00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.name: Façade of the Palace of Mushatta
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.dates: AD 743–744; given by the Ottoman sultan ‘Abd al-Hamid II to Emperor Wilhelm II in 1903
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.author: Stefan Weber
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.second_name: Decorative entrance facade of the Umayyad caliphal palace
00c2f038-d775-56aa-a8e0-bba81f9f6642.description2: The Umayyad palace façade of Mushatta – gifted by Ottoman sultan `Abd al-Hamid II – is one of the key works of Islamic art and a prime example of shared heritage. The monument shows the origins of a cultural era rooting in the various local traditions of Late Antiquity and also its early development. It hence became seminal for the Islamic art department, whose very establishment by Wilhelm von Bode in 1904 is due to this gift.

00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.name: The Hijaz Railway construction workers
00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.dates: Late 19th century – begining of the 20th century
00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph The Hijaz Railways
00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the interruption of the construction works caused by the outbreak of World War I.

00eecee6-1a79-5ca4-885a-64eb797adc19.name: *The bas-reliefs of Trajan's Column, reproduced in electroplating and exhibited in a room of the new Louvre*
00eecee6-1a79-5ca4-885a-64eb797adc19.second_name: Taken from the collection *Topographie de Paris*, "1er arrondissement, 1er quartier, Le Louvre"
00eecee6-1a79-5ca4-885a-64eb797adc19.description2: Trajan's Column, erected in Rome, is famous for its exceptional bas-reliefs commemorating the victory of the Emperor over the Dacians. In 1861, with the aim of making it known to the French public, Napoléon III had the column moulded and a replica installed in Paris. This was achieved thanks to the new electroplating technique, and the copy was placed in the Musée du Louvre. However, in 1870 the column was judged too large, and was sent to the Château de Saint-Germain, where it was quickly installed in the moat. In this image shows visitors at the Louvre, examining the story reproduced by Trajan's Column.

01e7089c-8585-5199-92a7-c9b05620637b.name: [Paris] stock exchange
01e7089c-8585-5199-92a7-c9b05620637b.description2: This building (Palais Brongniart), located in the heart of Paris, housed the French stock exchange for almost two centuries. Its atmosphere, as a powerful financial building bearing witness to great bankers' fortunes and failures, inspired writers such as Honoré de Balzac in La Maison Nucingen and Émile Zola in L’Argent.

025b84b0-d00d-5c21-a749-98f3596f9d77.name: Boots
025b84b0-d00d-5c21-a749-98f3596f9d77.description: Men’s leather riding boots. The applications of leather in different colours, with representation of geometric patterns, follow the customs and superstitions of the Hausa. The Hausa possessed, in every community, workshops for producing and dyeing articles of leather, though the most out-standing locations are those of Kano and Sokoto in Nigeria; places producing, since the medieval times, the thinnest skins used in Europe. The skins are those of goat, preferably of the males, and the dye receives the local name of *bagaruwa*. This product is usually processed by women, and it is also used for treating dysentery. The products of the Hausa are distributed, by trade, across wide zones of the Sahel and Subsaharian Africa.

03194f3e-048b-5d3e-a6af-514f37ac800f.name: Winged colossus
03194f3e-048b-5d3e-a6af-514f37ac800f.description2: Massive Assyrian winged animals captured the imagination of Victorian England. Large scale reproductions of them were incorporated into “The Assyrian Court” at the Crystal Palace Exhibition.

03762b34-622e-5cca-85b2-11ca849dd5d2.name: The Hijaz Railway delegations
03762b34-622e-5cca-85b2-11ca849dd5d2.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
03762b34-622e-5cca-85b2-11ca849dd5d2.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
03762b34-622e-5cca-85b2-11ca849dd5d2.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph The Hijaz Railways
03762b34-622e-5cca-85b2-11ca849dd5d2.description2: The Hijaz Railway ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj annual pilgrimage. Another important reason was to improve the economic and political integration of the distant Arabian provinces into the Ottoman state, and to facilitate the transportation of military forces.

04456e8e-b665-5aa7-96a4-825dc6689071.name: Near Eastern and Balkan map
04456e8e-b665-5aa7-96a4-825dc6689071.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
04456e8e-b665-5aa7-96a4-825dc6689071.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph map
04456e8e-b665-5aa7-96a4-825dc6689071.description2: One of the world's largest photo archives, Abdülhamid II's photo archives – knows as the Yildiz Albums – contain about 37 thousand pictures from that period of the Ottoman Empire. Abdülhamid II was the 34th Sultan of the Ottoman Empire and the last Sultan to exert effective autocratic control over the fracturing state. He oversaw a period of decline in the power and extent of the empire, including widespread pogroms and government massacres against the minorities of the empire (named the Hamidian massacres, after him) as well as an assassination attempt. He ruled from 31 August 1876 until he was deposed shortly after the 1908 Young Turk Revolution, on 27 April 1909.

057b0a91-5753-5a0f-a506-60b096d9eeb0.name: Saliha Sultan Fountain
057b0a91-5753-5a0f-a506-60b096d9eeb0.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
057b0a91-5753-5a0f-a506-60b096d9eeb0.description2: Robertson’s photographs of landscapes and monuments were usually printed in a roughly 25 by 30cm format. In the early years of his career as a photographer, he appears to have preferred the albumen-on-glass method of taking negatives, switching to the wet collodion process around 1855. For his positive prints, he used salt paper until about 1858; after that, prints were made on albumen paper even if they were made from negatives taken before that year. Robertson’s photographs are concentrated mainly in and around the districts known as Sultanahmet, Beyoğlu, Galata and Tophane today. This photo captures the Saliha Sultan Fountain in Galata.

0659eb21-0d9f-5b11-ae51-0ba0f6eea1f1.name: Reverent Baboon with Pharaoh figure
0659eb21-0d9f-5b11-ae51-0ba0f6eea1f1.description: The loud rejoicing of the Hamadryas baboon at the sunrise in its rocky habitat served as a model for the Egyptian celebration of the ascent and descent of the sun at the critical stages of its cycle. Baboons with upraised hands – the Egyptian gesture of reverence – became symbols for the “eastern souls”, the gods who cheer the sun at its appearance above the horizon. The king joins these gods in his role as sun priest.
0659eb21-0d9f-5b11-ae51-0ba0f6eea1f1.dates: 18th Dyn. Amenophis II, 1454-1419 BC; acquired in 1865/66
0659eb21-0d9f-5b11-ae51-0ba0f6eea1f1.dimensions: Height 130 cm, Width 42 cm, Diameter 61,5 cm

069c2465-1b42-5572-8535-19f44b1fc837.name: Archaeological excavations
069c2465-1b42-5572-8535-19f44b1fc837.description2:
This photograph shows the entrance to a tomb in the region of al-Kouban in Nubia, one of the archaeological sites excavated by James E. Quibell in 1882. The tomb has a vaulted ceiling made of mud brick, and the entrance marks the expansion of the tomb building from the inside.  
The photo is from a gelatine print negative, and it was included in the archive of the archaeological area of Saqqara, Giza.

06aabaa5-8fbd-543d-ac79-07b3315474de.name: The Statue of The God Bes
06aabaa5-8fbd-543d-ac79-07b3315474de.keywords: Istanbul Archaeological Museum; Tiled Kiosk; The God Bes
06aabaa5-8fbd-543d-ac79-07b3315474de.description2: A large statue of dwarf God Bes is located in the Aessos Works Hall. Bes was an ancient Egyptian dwarf god. He was a complex being who was both a deity and a demonic fighter. He was a god of war, yet he was also a patron of childbirth and the home, and was associated with sexuality, humour, music and dancing. Bes also became popular with the Phoenicians and in Cyprus.

07024cd6-c5bb-5d57-96ec-903ad7f248c4.name: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico “L. Pigorini” (National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography), Exhibition Room
07024cd6-c5bb-5d57-96ec-903ad7f248c4.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
07024cd6-c5bb-5d57-96ec-903ad7f248c4.author: Mario Mineo, Marina Minozzi
07024cd6-c5bb-5d57-96ec-903ad7f248c4.keywords: Paleoethnology; archaeology; exploration; anthropology; natural history; material culture; academy; Jesuits; Egypt; Egyptology; collection; collector; exoticism; curiosities; wunderkammer; Museum Kircherianum; Baroque; languages; Arabic
07024cd6-c5bb-5d57-96ec-903ad7f248c4.materials: Silver bromide negative impressed on glass
07024cd6-c5bb-5d57-96ec-903ad7f248c4.third_name: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico 'L. Pigorini', sala espositiva
07024cd6-c5bb-5d57-96ec-903ad7f248c4.description2:
The origins, in terms of scientific activity and conservation, of the Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the “Regio Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico di Roma" (Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography). Initially the museum was located in a wing of the Palazzo del Collegio Romano built in the late 16th century by the Society of Jesus.  
This rare image represents the old arrangement of one of the rooms of the Roman College, where the collection of antiquities and curiosities gathered together by Father Athanasius Kircher was kept after the foundation of the museum. According to the intentions of its founder, Luigi Pigorini, the purpose of this new institution was not only to gather together the remains of Italian prehistoric culture and the "primitive" cultures of other European and non-European peoples in a "central" museum located in the new capital of the Kingdom, but above all to support, promote and participate in research by paleontologists in Italy.

0801264d-8475-5c87-a800-17b6d0cc190e.name: The drawings of Janissary clothes from The Album of Mecmua-i Tesavir-i Osmaniye (The collection of Ottoman Pictures)
0801264d-8475-5c87-a800-17b6d0cc190e.holder: Military Museum and Cultural Centre Command
0801264d-8475-5c87-a800-17b6d0cc190e.description2: Arif Mehmed Pasha is considered one of the leaders of the western style of painting in Turkey. He developed a talent for drawing and produced a series of pictures detailing the clothes Ottoman state officials wore. He prepared these pictures under the name *Mecmua-i Tesavir-i Osmaniyye*. Although his work was supposed to come out in 12 volumes, only one volume was actually published in French in Paris in 1863 and in Turkish the same year. The other 11 volumes have been lost. The published volume is considered to be the first illustrated book in Turkey. What is amazing is the praise heaped onto Arif Mehmed Pasha for his portraits, the harmony of their colours and tones, the maturity of attitude and delicate detail, the artist’s control over his pen and watercolours. The clothing reflects the time when the Janissaries were still on the scene (before 1826 when the corps was disbanded).

0942d14e-52ed-5b05-a15c-0c47cf1ea748.name: Map of the Kingdoms of Fez and Morocco
0942d14e-52ed-5b05-a15c-0c47cf1ea748.description: A map drawn in the early 18th century to a scale of 1:50, its toponyms are in French.
0942d14e-52ed-5b05-a15c-0c47cf1ea748.keywords: Map; historical maps; French in Morocco; international relations; diplomacy; Moroccan-French relations; economy; trade; Moroccan-European relations; export; traditional economy; sea route; maritime route

094da4a9-5680-587b-b052-da54115ec7f0.name: Archaeological excavations
094da4a9-5680-587b-b052-da54115ec7f0.description2: This photograph shows a group of German scholars preparing reports of their excavation in the archaeological area of Saqqara. The picture dates to 1901. The original photograph was kept in the German Archive (an archive that the German archaeological mission left in Cairo).

09c3258d-f288-5759-b1ca-2328bd59ff7d.name: Cordless telephone; receiver with three pipes
09c3258d-f288-5759-b1ca-2328bd59ff7d.artist: Agence de Presse Meurisse (Meurisse Press Agency)
09c3258d-f288-5759-b1ca-2328bd59ff7d.description2: After the invention of the telephone in the 1860s, inventors began to try and find ways to move over to "wireless" telephones. Some solutions emerged at the end of the 19th century, but as this photograph from 1919 demonstrates, the equipment was still far too cumbersome to be used comfortably.

0b7f2149-f01d-5891-815e-947600259db6.name: *The drilling of an artesian well*
0b7f2149-f01d-5891-815e-947600259db6.artist: Artist: G. Dascher; engraver: L. Geisler
0b7f2149-f01d-5891-815e-947600259db6.description2: The purpose of the album *Les Colonies Françaises* was to highlight, amongst other things, the French "achievements" and technological innovations in the colonies, and thus legitimise their rule. This image shows the construction of an artesian well in Tunisia in the 19th century. In reality, however, this type of well was built by the French army in order to appease the populations in agricultural areas and thus better control them.

0ba224c3-c5fc-59df-943c-70ba396625a7.name: Lambaesis. Inside the praetorium
0ba224c3-c5fc-59df-943c-70ba396625a7.description2: This photograph belonged to Georges Sirot (1898–1977), one of the first great collectors of photographs. Lambaesis was a military town in Roman Africa, rediscovered by archaeologists.

0bdb3920-5c44-5859-a7de-be6f63a099b9.name: *Raft Conveying Winged Bull to Baghdad*
0bdb3920-5c44-5859-a7de-be6f63a099b9.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
0bdb3920-5c44-5859-a7de-be6f63a099b9.description2: Layard describes the removal of the winged bulls from the site of the mound of Nimrud in Nineveh and its remains, 1849, from where they had lain for approximately the last 2,730 years. They were carefully loaded on to rafts, made in the traditional way of using hundreds of inflated goat and sheep-skins supporting a wooden superstructure. Layard (who had learnt Arabic and Persian) recruited the crew locally, as he had done with his workforce. In April 1847, he sent them floating with the current, off on a six hundred mile journey down the river Tigris to Basra, where ships of the British Navy were waiting to take them the next 12,000 miles to England. Although the artist Cooper was not present on this occasion, he subsequently witnessed similar events, and would have been able to reconstruct the scene.

0c667bca-0934-5597-9606-a0052b8b5720.name: *Cairo, the Nile Dam*
0c667bca-0934-5597-9606-a0052b8b5720.second_name: Taken from Marcel Jusserand, *Souvenirs d'Egypte* (Memories of Egypt)
0c667bca-0934-5597-9606-a0052b8b5720.description2: The reign of Muhammad 'Ali Pasha was marked by a series of great changes, including attempts to take control of irrigation. The governor appointed French specialists, amongst whom was Linant de Bellefonds, and tasked them with the construction of a dam near Cairo. Linant de Bellefonds faced a great many difficulties during the construction, such as saving the pyramids, which the Pasha had wanted to destroy in order to supply the new dam with stone. The works were taken over by the engineer Eugène Mougel who added fortifications, as can be seen from this photograph, taken by a tourist at the beginning of the 20th century. The dam was completed c. 1835.

0dc391d9-1f9b-5c22-91bf-a9670c98fa1b.name: Two Egyptian mummies
0dc391d9-1f9b-5c22-91bf-a9670c98fa1b.dates: Undated; 1906 (included in the National Museum of Antiquities collection)
0dc391d9-1f9b-5c22-91bf-a9670c98fa1b.description2: The National Museum of Antiquities was founded in Wallachia in 1834. According to a museum catalogue from 1906, a section of one exhibition room was dedicated to “Egyptian religious objects” (more than 120 items, among which small statues of various gods and goddesses, amulets, clay or bronze scarabs, cameos, a mummified hand). The museum also owned three mummies, exhibited in the “Trophy Room”, along with very varied objects of different epochs. Two of the mummies, belonging to a little boy and girl, were donated by a certain captain Horovitz (no information about him is known), who brought them from Cairo. He also offered the museum a mummified ibis and four mummified parrots.

0e467a26-3229-554d-8707-115f086aa0be.name: Portrait of Claudius Rich
0e467a26-3229-554d-8707-115f086aa0be.keywords: Bible; travelling; archaeology; archaeological excavation; exploration; collecting; collector; museums
0e467a26-3229-554d-8707-115f086aa0be.description2: Rich was the East India Company’s first Resident in Baghdad. He was a talented linguist. In his spare time he explored ancient sites, producing the first proper plans of Babylon and Nineveh. He hosted important travellers to Iraq, searching for sites of Biblical relevance. In 1821 he died during a cholera outbreak in Shiraz. His collection formed the nucleus of the British Museum’s collection.

0e6a50b3-2b5c-5608-aae5-77ecf66cfde2.name: *Sketch of Algeria, featuring the Roman occupation, the railway lines, roads suitable for mule and horse drawn vehicles, ports* \[…\] drawn from an archaeological point of view and dedicated to ...
0e6a50b3-2b5c-5608-aae5-77ecf66cfde2.second_name: Taken from *Revue Africaine: Journal des Travaux de la Société Historique Algérienne 78*
0e6a50b3-2b5c-5608-aae5-77ecf66cfde2.description2: Founded in 1856, the Société Historique Algérienne organised excavations, published a journal, and created maps and plans. This map helped facilitate research on the Roman occupation of Algeria, by indicating clearly the main sites, how to get there, and other elements which allow the reader to better understand the Roman presence (such as marble quarries and thermal baths).

0f2af30a-b903-5cfa-a52e-5a834629196d.name: *Sbeïtla. Attempt to reconstruct the façade of the three temples*
0f2af30a-b903-5cfa-a52e-5a834629196d.second_name: Description of the antiquities of the Tunisian regency: monuments from before the Arab conquest. Report on the 1882–83 mission.
0f2af30a-b903-5cfa-a52e-5a834629196d.description2: The French architect and winner of the Grand Prix de Rome, Henri Saladin, went on an archaeological campaign to Tunisia with the archaeologist René Cagnat between 1882 and 1883. He took many sketches in various archaeological sites, such as this drawing of Sbeïtla (the ancient Roman city in Sufetula). Upon his return he constructed a "Tunisian pavilion" for the 1889 Exposition Universelle (world fair) in Paris, which contained a mix of all the different architectural styles he had seen during his time in Tunisia.

1028751a-07f0-53c2-8d14-e1b298d6e008.name: Board
1028751a-07f0-53c2-8d14-e1b298d6e008.description: Qur'anic board used in the African *madrasas* (schools), places where the first verses of the Qur'an are learned, under the direction of the *marabout* (teacher). The learning method consists of copying and reciting the different verses of the Qur'an, in a process of memorisation, which allows the students to erase them and then to write the following verses. The *alluha* (table of wood), the reed, and the ink are the only available pedagogic materials of the Qur'anic schools in the rural areas. The Qur'anic boards turn into documents that preserve the written personality of those who used them, the irregularity of the letter, the crooked lines, the hesitations, the corrected mistakes, the erased lines that refuse to disappear, as a register of a period of effort and domain of skills typical of the school stage.

104473a3-fc89-55f7-a3b9-20138dba554c.name: Plan of the city of Pompeii and the excavations there, pl. 2. Historical note
104473a3-fc89-55f7-a3b9-20138dba554c.second_name: Taken from *Dessins des Ruines de Pompéi*
104473a3-fc89-55f7-a3b9-20138dba554c.description2: The architect François Mazois (1783–1826) was appointed as Caroline Murat's official artist in 1809. He was allowed to set up in Pompeii to draw and measure the ruins, something unheard of at this time. His drawings and observations, published under the title *Les Ruines de Pompéi, Dessinées et Mesurées pendant les Années 1809 à 1811*, became a model for contemporary archaeologists and a source of inspiration for neo-Classical architecture.

11882e61-41ff-533d-8ba1-acb37292e9e4.name: The Rosetta Stone
11882e61-41ff-533d-8ba1-acb37292e9e4.keywords: archaeology; Egyptomania; exploration; collection; collecting; museums; inscription; Greek inscription; hieroglyph; Demotic; science
11882e61-41ff-533d-8ba1-acb37292e9e4.description2: An iconic image of decipherment, since the same text is inscribed in three different scripts, including Greek, the ‘stone’ is actually part of a grey and pink granodiorite stela bearing a priestly decree concerning Ptolemy V in three blocks of text: Hieroglyphic (14 lines), Demotic (32 lines) and Greek (54 lines).

124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.name: Port of Beirut
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.description: The Port of Beirut is the main port in Lebanon and it is one of the most beneficial commercial architecture in Lebanon that contributes the state’s revenue. It was founded in 1887 under the reign of the Ottomans and has since been the western-eastern link in the Middle East area. The Port of Beirut has a total area of 1,200,000 m2.
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.holder: Government of Lebanon; Gestation and exploitation of Port of Beirut (GEPB)
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem, Julien El Khoury
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.history: Founded in 1887, the Port of Beirut is located on the eastern side of St Georges Bay, on Beirut's northern Mediterranean coast, west of the Beirut river. It is one of the largest and busiest ports of the Eastern Mediterranean. In early 90’s, a phase of development and reconstruction took place. The Port was rehabilitated and expanded to encompass 4 docks, 2 new quays (15 and 16) and new container terminal with 700,000 TEU/year capacities. The container terminal became operational in February 2005. It is equipped with 6 ship-to-shore gantry cranes (outreach 60m) and 18 rubbed tyred gantry cranes. The Port of Beirut has been selected as a transhipment hub for the 2nd and 3rd largest container shipping companies in the world.

130aa879-2175-5e76-b109-ed289b2b585e.name: Roman tomb (columbarium),  Marengo gardens, Bab el-Oued

139d89ef-83f7-5902-8e15-21a9ae45cbf2.name: Early collecting
139d89ef-83f7-5902-8e15-21a9ae45cbf2.description2: A colossal statue of Cypriot Bes was found near the agora of the ancient city of Amathus in 1863. The British government attempted to obtain it for the British Museum but it was sent to Constantinople on order of the Porte. This illustrates the beginnings of a more official policy to claim antiquities for the Ottoman state and to exhibit them in museums. The first Ottoman Law on antiquities was passed in 1869, followed by a more detailed one in 1874.

13a6be55-80b1-576f-be99-bfc3e15b7c3f.name: *Casket from San Isidoro of León*
13a6be55-80b1-576f-be99-bfc3e15b7c3f.description: This casket was donated by the Dean of Leon Cathedral to the National Museum of Archaeology in 1869. It was part of the Cathedral Treasury and it is an example of the importance of Arab workshops in the Iberian Peninsula in Middle Ages.

13c7b9a9-f604-53fe-8a42-508a3f774e73.description2: General view of the pyramids of Abusir with a group of workers excavating the pyramids of Sahure and Niuserre as part of the German archaeological mission in 1901.

147b289f-3d6e-58be-8aa0-db105cfb150f.name: *National Museum of Archaeology No. 9 (Arab Courtyard) Monuments and Epigraphy of Islamic Spain*
147b289f-3d6e-58be-8aa0-db105cfb150f.description: View of the courtyard in the National Museum of Archaeology, also known as "Arab courtyard", between 1917-1936. This room displayed different pieces such as the Alfajería arch, a copy of the fountain of the Lions and the bronze lamp from the Alhambra palace. This room was one of the first museum galleries focusing on Arab or Islamic pieces in Europe.

1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.name: Perpetual calendar
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.dimensions: Height 130 mm, width 70 mm, depth 33 mm
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.materials: Nielloed silver, copper alloy, iron, wood, printed paper, printed textile
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.description2: This perpetual calendar is contained within a cylindrical silver casing with a rounded shoulder. Four lateral knobs, two on either side, move the calendar's paper and textile elements, giving the month, the date and probably the day (this section is damaged). Above, a circular medallion contains the start year of the calendar, 1327 H/ 1909 AD.  The calendar is decorated all over with delicate niello deccoration. The front, with three superposed and elongated cartouche-shaped openings, is ornamented with a lobed panel containing naturalistic flower sprays. Below, a panel with three loop extensions contains an Arabic inscription - taqweem da'imi - that identifies the object's function. In the Tanzimat period, and up to 1926, the Mailya or Rumi calendar was introduced, which was based on the Julian solar calendar but started in the year of the Prophet's (pbuh) move from Makkah to Madina in 1 H/ 622 AD. It used old Syrian names for the months and was intended to ease the annual tax and fiscal calculations and payments.

14fa7435-2efe-5c6f-be7f-cc253ffd3d64.name: A historical fake
14fa7435-2efe-5c6f-be7f-cc253ffd3d64.keywords: Cuneiform; archaeology; exploration; archaeology; museums; collection; collector; travel; traveller; inscription
14fa7435-2efe-5c6f-be7f-cc253ffd3d64.description2: An early example of a fake antiquity. It was made by impressing a real tablet into new clay. The typology of fakes has changed as our familiarity with and understanding of tablets has grown.

154a0f2d-b51b-50e4-a764-5552e98c9b1a.name: A photo of the Irrigation Room at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
154a0f2d-b51b-50e4-a764-5552e98c9b1a.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photo taken during the inauguration of the museum)
154a0f2d-b51b-50e4-a764-5552e98c9b1a.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

17926a9d-a6e5-5215-b39f-488c46d6e51c.name: *Firman*
17926a9d-a6e5-5215-b39f-488c46d6e51c.keywords: archaeology; exploration; Egyptomania; collection; collector; travel; traveller; museums; historical document; imperial symbols; Ottoman monograms
17926a9d-a6e5-5215-b39f-488c46d6e51c.description2: The official permit, or *firman*, confirming the appointment of Henry Salt to the post of British Consul in Egypt, dated 23 December 1815. The imperial cipher at the top is flanked by floral motifs. This is a fine manuscript with exquisite Arabic calligraphy and watercolour and gold floral decorations. When Salt arrived in Egypt in 1816 he obtained permission from the Pasha, Mohammed Ali, to collect antiquities for the British Museum.

17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.name: Uadi-Merdùm [Wadi Merdum]. Count Sforza and the Interpreter Maffei Transcribe a Roman Inscription Brought to their Attention by 'Natives'
17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.author: Patrizia Pampana, Giulia Barrera
17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.third_name: *Uadi-Merdùm. Il conte Sforza e l’interprete Maffei trascrivono un’iscrizione romana segnalata dagli indigeni*
17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.second_name: The members of an Italian mission to Libya, aimed at assessing local mining resources, transcribe a Roman inscription
17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.description2:
In 1911, before the war broke out, Count Sforza and Ignazio Sanfilippo were touring Libya on a mission to assess local resources, sponsored by the Libyan branch of the Banco di Roma. Their parallel interest in Roman archaeology – testified by this photo – is meaningful for the connection between Italians’ claims of their Roman heritage and Italian colonial ambitions.  
In the opinion of Italian colonialists the discovery of Roman antiquities in Libya brought support to Italian argument that Italy had an historic right to rule over Libya.

18197caa-f988-5826-9a1d-d30e87a0bed4.name: Ottoman map of the period of Sultan Abdülhamid II
18197caa-f988-5826-9a1d-d30e87a0bed4.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
18197caa-f988-5826-9a1d-d30e87a0bed4.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph map
18197caa-f988-5826-9a1d-d30e87a0bed4.description2: One of the world's largest photo archives, Abdülhamid II's photo archives – knows as the Yildiz Albums – contain about 37 thousand pictures from that period of the Ottoman Empire. Abdülhamid II was the 34th Sultan of the Ottoman Empire and the last Sultan to exert effective autocratic control over the fracturing state. He oversaw a period of decline in the power and extent of the empire, including widespread pogroms and government massacres against the minorities of the empire (named the Hamidian massacres, after him) as well as an assassination attempt. He ruled from 31 August 1876 until he was deposed shortly after the 1908 Young Turk Revolution, on 27 April 1909.

18fa1217-5885-554f-bf5c-aed5d4898cb0.name: Editorial. Inauguration of the Musée Gallo-Romain at the Château de Saint-Germain
18fa1217-5885-554f-bf5c-aed5d4898cb0.keywords: Gallo-roman antiquities; Musée de Sain-Germain en Laye
18fa1217-5885-554f-bf5c-aed5d4898cb0.description2: In March 1862, Emperor Napoléon III ordered the "creation of a museum for Celtic and Gallo-Roman antiquities at the Château de Saint-Germain-en-Laye". The castle was restored by Eugène Millet, student of Viollet-le-Duc, who chose to restore it to its condition under François I. A team of confirmed archaeologists were tasked with the organisation of the Museum. Napoléon III wanted a museum dedicated to the archaeology of the national lands (contrary to the collections at the Louvre), and methodically classified: the first curator, Alexandre Bertrand, introduced a chronological classification, breaking the tradition of thematically classified collections. The emperor chose to inaugurate the museum with a symbolically extravagant ceremony, while in Paris the Exposition Universelle (world fair) was in full swing (May 1867).

18fd68f6-0db6-5ad7-aa02-07fc4aa8572e.name: Bronze medal celebrating the Suez Canal
18fd68f6-0db6-5ad7-aa02-07fc4aa8572e.description2: This medal combines two of the great passions of the late 19th century: modern technology (here in the form of the magnificent new canal) and the captivating remains of ancient Egypt.

1947528b-a97f-56af-b6c4-fe8372c9bdd5.name: *The Western Wall*
1947528b-a97f-56af-b6c4-fe8372c9bdd5.description2: The Western Wall of the Haram es-Sharif in Jerusalem, as depicted for the readers of the Illustrated London News by William ‘Crimea’ Simpson. Simpson’s sketches were turned into engravings for publication in the ILN, and were among the most important graphic depictions which helped to introduce western readers to the present-day appearance of Jerusalem and Jerusalemites.

1959666e-3460-5e95-bc55-a3706388cf52.name: Archaeological excavations
1959666e-3460-5e95-bc55-a3706388cf52.description2: This photograph documents the discovery and excavation of archaeological relics in the area of Saqqara in 1901. The original photograph was included in a specific collection of the German Archive.

1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.name: *Exposition Universelle - Their Royal Imperial Majesties and the Viceroy of Egypt visit the Temple of Edfu*
1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.artist: Artist: Filippo Liardo; illustrator: Gustave Janet
1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.keywords: Archaeological excavations; Egyptomania; Egypt; World fairs
1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.description2: Visitors to the 1867 Exposition Universelle (world fair) had the opportunity to explore a reconstruction of the Temple of Edfu in a "Parc Égyptien". This reconstruction (containing a mix of various different temples) was a response both to the fashion for ancient Egypt, and the desire for good diplomatic relations with modern Egypt. Indeed, we can see the imperial couple in this photograph standing with Isma'il Pasha, the viceroy of Egypt, who had come to see the exhibition. The Temple of Edfu had just been rediscovered by the famous Egyptologist Mariette.

1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.holder: Musée des Postes, Télégraphes et Télécommunications
1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.keywords: Post and telegraph office; Greco-Roman style
1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.description2: This oil on canvas painting shows a scene from daily life at the Tunis post and telegraph office, built on the Rue d'Italie (now Rue Charles-de-Gaulle). One of the busiest rooms, the revenue office's great hall is, with its tremendously high ceilings, an impressive example of neo-classical architecture. Featuring elements of carved plaster and a map of Tunisia on a central marble panel, this painting faithfully reproduces the opulence of this historic building.

1c4b95a5-1ef1-50b3-a51a-bdc1148ce5c5.description2: Photograph showing workers at the site of the excavations carried out in the area of Abusir in 1901, and the discovery of some archaeological pieces and columns. Photo taken by the German archaeological mission.

1e5a98c0-6a45-5ac8-8201-22da00b4e53b.description2: General view of the pyramids of Abusir, in the area of the pyramids of the king Userkaf and king Neferirkare. These pyramids represent vestiges of the Fifth Dynasty, and they date back to 2800 BC (Old Kingdom). The paper photograph is printed from glass plate negatives.

1e650671-cb20-50f3-8f15-8ed06e41849a.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies

1e650671-cb20-50f3-8f15-8ed06e41849a.second_name: An old Greek woman who was the only person remaining in the Libyan town Marsa Susa when the Italian army occupied it
1e650671-cb20-50f3-8f15-8ed06e41849a.description2:
This picture was taken by an Italian military unit during the Italian invasion of Libya.  
Apollonia was the name of an ancient town, dating back to the 7th century BC. By 1911, Apollonia was nothing more than an archaeological site. The modern Arab town was called Marsa Susa. The Italians’ use of the ancient name was intended to remind readers that Libya was once under Roman rule. Italian colonialists claimed that Italy had an historic right to rule over Libya, since the Roman Empire once ruled over that country.

1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.location: Northwest of Saudi Arabia in al-'Ula (Alula) region
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.history: Historically the Tribe of Lihyan was the first known Tribe settled in the area and founded the Kingdom of Lihyan in the "Oasis of Aula" in  the sixth century until the fourth BC. There is not much historical information about the Lihyanite but mentions that they allied themselves with the Nabataeans later. The largest settlement in the area was in the first century AD when the Nabateans made it as the second capital of  their kingdom after Petra in Jordan. The Nabateans dug their graves in the facades  of the mountains of the region , where there are about 132 tombs cut and carved in the rock. Nabataean state has fallen at the hands of the Romans in the second century AD.
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.keywords: Railway; station; Hijaz railway; Arabian Peninsula; history of the Hijaz railway; communication; innovation; route; pilgrimage; hajj; Ottoman; Germany; Abdul Hamid; abd al-hamid

1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.description2: Mada'in Salih Station, which is located 25 kilometres north-east of al-'Ula City, was one of the main railway stations. The site contains seventeen building in addition to the ancient Islamic castle, and there is an old water pool and five wells folded with stones, as well as sixteen building of the railway station have been built in trimmed stones. The buildings had been converted into a museum tells the history of the Hijaz Railway.

1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; History of Water in Ottoman Empire; Water; map
1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The Cendere Hamidian Water Pump Station was built by Abdülhamid II in 1902. The station is located at an altitude of 34 metres above sea level. With its function, architectural design and mechanical equipment, the station is a unique reminder of Ottoman architecture. It pumped to Balmumcu and Beşiktaş – with water coming from 20 different pipes in Kağıthane, propelled by steam pump machines.

201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.name: Disk
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.dates: New Kingdom (16th–11th century BC); discovered in 1824
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.dimensions: Diameter 7.2 cm; length of the golden foil 4,6 cm; glass thickness 0,6 cm
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.author: Marina Minozzi
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.description2: The disk in green glass with a golden square foil is considered of remarkable interest because of its label, attributed to Ippolito Rosellini, which proves that the relic was found inside a tomb in Thebes. Rosellini, one of the main figures of the Franco-Tuscan expedition in Egypt, wrote on it "Disco di vetro con entro una lamina d'oro. Trovato in una tomba a Tebe, Egitto, da I. Rosellini 1824 -dono di Elenina Ox Sicard, dicembre 1902". The relic was later acquired by Enrico Hillyer Giglioli. As a result of the excavations by W. Petrie and J. De Morgan, who documented the existence of an era preceding the 1st dynasty, Luigi Pigorini decided to expand the Egyptian archaeological collection in the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano" which he directed at that time. In 1878 he began to acquire important groups, with the main body of the collection donated by David Randall-MacIver in 1901, after the excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. Another major purchase — from the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin — followed in 1905. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from the Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.

en: Cappozzo, M., “La collezione egizia del Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico ‘Luigi Pigorini’”, in *Bullettino di Paletnologia Italiana*, Roma, Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato, (2005–2007), 96: 131–202, cat. 154.

2088a0e4-bb93-514d-9d8c-6b0a1e09ef8a.name: *The Necropolis, Petra, March 9th, 1839*
2088a0e4-bb93-514d-9d8c-6b0a1e09ef8a.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
2088a0e4-bb93-514d-9d8c-6b0a1e09ef8a.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
2088a0e4-bb93-514d-9d8c-6b0a1e09ef8a.description2: The Necropolis' of Petra appears in Volume 3 of 'The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia' from drawings made on the spot by David Roberts, lithographed by Louis Haghe and published in six volumes by F.G. Moon in London between 1842-1845. Situated at the beginning of the steep ravine or siq that leads into the heart of Petra, both the so-called 'obelisk tomb' shown in the centre and the Triclinium situated to its lower right still exist today, even if much eroded since the days Roberts visited Petra in 1839. In the 19th century, Petra was one of Europe's most enduring Orientalist fascinations, but it also played a part in the region's more modern history. In October 1917, T. E. Lawrence, to divert Turkish military resources away from the British advance before the Third Battle of Gaza, led a small force of Syrians and Arabs in successfully defending Petra against a combined force of Turks and Germans. Bedouin women from the Petra area - under the leadership of their Sheikh's wife - were recruited to fight in the defense of the city.

21b91c4b-40fa-5696-96fc-cfe01762acda.name: A Khorsabad barrel
21b91c4b-40fa-5696-96fc-cfe01762acda.dates: 721–705 BC (reign of Sargon II); discovered in 1851–1854
21b91c4b-40fa-5696-96fc-cfe01762acda.description2: During the archaeological mission led in Khorsabad by French consul Victor Place (1851–1854), fourteen Assyrian barrels were discovered. However, only four were preserved, since most of Place’s findings were lost in a shipwreck that took place in April 1855 on the Shatt el-Arab. As a reward for his archeological activity, the French government offered Place one of the barrels. Between 1855-1863 he was a consul in Moldavia, where he settled and started a family. In 1987 the Romanian state bought the barrel from one of Place’s descendants after the authorities found out that he was trying to sell it abroad. The barrel is made of clay, is nine-sided and bears an inscription recounting the reign of Assyrian king Sargon II, founder of a new capital, Dur-Sharrukin (Khorsabad).

22ba355b-61ed-56c7-97f9-3b2325767140.description2: *The Railway Station at Jaffa* is a drawing included in the book *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine. In the chapters about Jaffa and Jerusalem, the description of the geography, religious history and climate focuses on the route of the Jaffa–Jerusalem railway. It provides an interesting report on this communication route, built by the French and opened on September 1892, connecting Jaffa to Jerusalem and various villages in between.

26d5c466-64f0-57e3-823b-ed86f67a2c66.name: A postcard of Italian colonial propaganda
26d5c466-64f0-57e3-823b-ed86f67a2c66.description: The Roman Empire once ruled over the entire coastal area of North Africa. This postcard explicitly links the Italian colonial conquest of Libya in 1911-12 with ancient Roman rule over the same territory. It suggests that the Italian Kingdom was the legitimate heir of the Roman Empire and had an historic right to rule over Libya. Especially during Fascism, Italian colonial propaganda often referred to the Roman Empire in order to legitimize Italian expansionist policy.

275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

279d0dc2-0ffe-5cf8-89f7-8199c9c7ec9a.name: *Fantasy in Egyptian Gallery, the British Museum*
279d0dc2-0ffe-5cf8-89f7-8199c9c7ec9a.description2: Fantasy in Egyptian Gallery, the British Museum, by Duncan. A group of sculptures come to life. Closely modelled on the sculptures displayed in the British Museum. Assyrianising figures at rear left. At front right Ry yawns and rubs his eye.

27bffbe0-bf77-51b6-87f3-1667b65ae607.name: *The Ruins of the Temple of the Sun at Baalbec*
27bffbe0-bf77-51b6-87f3-1667b65ae607.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
27bffbe0-bf77-51b6-87f3-1667b65ae607.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
27bffbe0-bf77-51b6-87f3-1667b65ae607.description2: This dramatic view looks across the great court of the temple complex in Baalbek. In the ancient world Baalbek, to the east of Beirut in Lebanon, was a great centre of trade between Europe and Asias, and home to a religion of sun worship. The Scottish artist David Roberts visited in 1839 and over the following years made many images of the still imposing ruins. This painting is Roberts's last of Baalbek, and he considered it as 'a grand finale' to his career as a painter of the Middle East. The complex's imposing architectural and artistic details also inspired European Neoclassical architects and artists such as Robert Adam. Since about 1864 many tourists visited the famed site, including, in 1898, the German emperor Wilhelm II on his way to Jerusalem. Struck by the magnificence of the ruins, he dispatched a German archaeological team, whose subsequent work resulted in a meticulously presented and illustrated publication that further raised interest in Baalbek.

27e660f6-6597-5bf6-8766-18aaf9b3ddc1.name: Petrie Stereo Photobook 1
27e660f6-6597-5bf6-8766-18aaf9b3ddc1.description2: Petrie was a pioneer of archaeological photography, even though at the time the technique of half-toning had not been developed, so that his photographs had to be turned into woodcuts for publication. He was a great believer in the importance of photography, and, at least at this time, took all of his archaeological photographs as stereo pairs, another of his pioneering works.

29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.name: *The Franco-Tuscan Expedition to Egypt*
29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.author: Marina Minozzi
29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.keywords: Campaign in Egypt; Egyptomania; archaeology; Leopoldo II; Charles X; scientific expedition; university; museums; collection; collector; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; epigraphy; Italian painters; travelling artist; botany
29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.copyright: Copyright image: Su concessione del Ministero per i Beni Culturali e del Turismo - Museo Egizio di Firenze.
29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.description2:
In 1827 the artist Giuseppe Angelelli took part in the Franco-Tuscan campaign to Egypt (1828–1829) sponsored by the French Government and the Grand Duke of Tuscany and directed by the archaeologist Ippolito Rosellini. Once back in Florence, the Grand Duke of Tuscany commissioned him to create a painting of those who took part at the campaign in Thebes.  
The two directors are represented in the core of the scene, wearing the Nizam, the official clothing, which has recently been required by the pasha and willingly adopted by most of them. Champollion is seated and Ippolito Rosellini is standing at his right, holding a sheet depicting one of the Kadesh Battle's scenes, that of Pharaoh grabbing an enemy's arm. In the middle, between the two protagonists, is the engineer Gaetano Rosellini, Ippolito's uncle and architect in charge of the two missions. On the left, several members of the Commissions: the elder Raddi, dressed in European garb and holding a lotus flower in his hand; the illustrator Duchesne is shown in the foreground with the colours on one side and a painting of ruins on the other.

2bcb43f7-b5d0-5c2b-a273-3d6e8643ed05.name: Mosaic of Virgil
2bcb43f7-b5d0-5c2b-a273-3d6e8643ed05.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
2bcb43f7-b5d0-5c2b-a273-3d6e8643ed05.description2: This mosaic shows Virgil listening to Clio and Melpomene. It was discovered in Sousse (ancient Hadrumetum) in 1896 and is one of the gems of the Musée du Bardo. Dressed in a splendid white toga decorated with gold embroidery, this mosaic is one of the most remarkable portraits of the famous Roman poet. He is surrounded by the muses Clio and Melpomene and holds a roll of parchment on his knee, on which the eighth verse of the Aeneid is written. The mosaic is the oldest representations of Virgil known today.

2be85362-6e14-5698-94e1-a895d7c03a8e.description2: Sgt. Birtles, Charles Warren’s chief assistant during the work in Jerusalem, climbing down into the destruction debris of Herod’s Temple in the Tyropoean Valley.

2beb8ede-81f6-5a62-aa22-de18127faa93.name: Photograph of Casablanca Railway Station
2beb8ede-81f6-5a62-aa22-de18127faa93.description: In 1908, the French General Albert d’Amade led the pacification of the Kabyle Berber peoples on the plains of Chaouia and also oversaw the construction of a railway line between Casablanca and Berrechid. By 1914, the railway was mainly used for the civil transportation of people and goods. This shot of Casablanca Station in 1920 depicts a train arriving at the station, where the passengers waiting to board appear to be European settlers and Moroccan notables.

2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.second_name: Great Mosque with the famous minaret (Malwiya) of the caliphal city of Samarra, groundbreaking excavation by E. Herzfeld 1911–13
2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.description2: Of great importance for the collection of the first Museum of Islamic Art in the western world are the findings made during the excavations in Samarra, which were conducted by Ernst Herzfeld and the museum’s first director, Friedrich Sarre, between 1911 and 1913. The study of the Abbasid’s temporal second capital has contributed to an understanding of the developments and changes in Islamic art at the time.

2f499780-f936-5142-8597-fc27d9b2d0ce.name: An old exhibition from Tiled Kiosk
2f499780-f936-5142-8597-fc27d9b2d0ce.dates: The Tiled Kiosk: 15th century; The photograph: 19th century
2f499780-f936-5142-8597-fc27d9b2d0ce.description2: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace and dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its closeness and those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.

2fd7dbb0-f684-52f4-93f3-b485ecf82f5e.name: Postcard: *The Strait of Gibraltar in the Future*
2fd7dbb0-f684-52f4-93f3-b485ecf82f5e.description: This curious postcard with a utopian vision of how the Strait of Gibraltar could become in the future was sent to the Marquis of Cerralbo by a friend, Gabriel Vich, but never received a stamp. Although it shows the address of the marquis, maybe it was posted inside an envelope or delivered, finally, on hand. This kind of ephemera was published by the fortnightly publication España en África (Spain in Africa), active in the first decades of the 20th century. The image represented is a beautiful commercial and geopolitical project that would have linked two continents with a 15 km bridge.

340abb76-0aa3-53e7-b9ea-c4ebf5b8737b.description2: The print reproduces the drawing, today at the University Library of Pisa, realised by Giuseppe Angelelli. Angelelli’s painting is used for Table LXXXIII of the Historical Monuments which shows one of the engraved paintings from the southern wall of the temple of Abu Simbel, celebrating King Ramses piercing his enemy with a spear. This is a traditional scene that has been reproduced on numerous Egyptian monuments from early historic periods to show the supremacy of the Pharaoh above all foreign people. The enemies of the Egyptians are characterised by libic hair and dresses. An error was made by the copier in the spear used by Rameses, possibly reproduced within Angelelli’s painting because of the Director of the Commission wanted to correct the hieroglyphical text above.

34ebe371-2a09-50f9-8e86-921fabe509cc.name: *Portico of the Temple at Edfu, Upper Egypt*
34ebe371-2a09-50f9-8e86-921fabe509cc.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
34ebe371-2a09-50f9-8e86-921fabe509cc.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
34ebe371-2a09-50f9-8e86-921fabe509cc.description2: Considered the best preserved cult temple of ancient Egypt, Edfu temple was swamped with sand in Roberts’s days, and houses had been built on top. The French archaeologist Auguste Mariette eventually excavated it in the 1860s.This view shows the temple's portico, its  sand-filled façade supported by six monumental columns. The columns on either side of the centre have large lotus columns, those flanking them are made to resemble vertically rising date palm fronds. The outermost columns carry capitals derived from composite Theban palm tree designs. Beyond the columns of the facade, two further rows of capitaled columns form the inner area of the portico, or pronaos. Over the entrance of the portico and on the upper shafts of the columns, pharaonic imagery, emblems, cartouches and hieroglyphs are clearly visible.  The artist emphasizes the monumentality of both the portico and the masses of sand that have invaded it by introducing a group of dwarfed visitors resting on one of the sand dunes in the centre – utterly dwarfed by their surroundings.

363a9b8e-3ef5-567b-a032-97afeab68478.description2: This photograph was taken by an unknown author during the excavations led by Ernesto Schiaparelli in Egypt. Schiaparelli (1856-1928) was Director of the Egyptian Museum of Florence from 1881 to 1894 and in 1894 became Director of the Egyptian Museum of Turin. The photograph shows a section of a trail in the south of Deir el-Bahri. It is easy to recognize the ruins of a residential district, which presumably hosted the workers and the artisans involved in the works for the tombs of the Valley of the Queens. Ernesto Schiaparelli, first as museum director and then as excavation superintendent from 1907 to his death, led several excavation campaigns around 1903-1914 in the Valley of the Queens, a place dedicated to the burial of wives, princes and princesses since the reign of Rameses I.

3834322c-3b30-5333-9de0-37e6dc5efe5d.name: The statue of Hadrian
3834322c-3b30-5333-9de0-37e6dc5efe5d.dates: The Tiled Kiosk: 15th century; the photograph: 19th century; emperor Hadrian: 76—138 A.D.
3834322c-3b30-5333-9de0-37e6dc5efe5d.description2: Hadrian was the fourteenth Emperor of Rome (10 August 117 to 10 July 138 CE) and is known as the third of the Five Good Emperors (Nerva, Trajan, Hadrian, Antoninus Pius, and Marcus Aurelius) who ruled justly. The statue of the famous Roman Emperor Hadrian is located in the Roman hall of the museum. Hadrian was depicted with a figure under his foot. The statue was found in Crete.

385662fc-85ab-5e90-a9e6-c6b945d3350c.name: Egyptian mummy
385662fc-85ab-5e90-a9e6-c6b945d3350c.dates: 22nd dynasty (c. 950–730 BC); beginning of the 20th century
385662fc-85ab-5e90-a9e6-c6b945d3350c.description2: Romanian politician and doctor Nicolae Kretzulescu, his wife and their daughter spent the winter of 1868-1869 in Egypt at the invitation of the German consul, whose wife was Mrs. Kretzulescu’s aunt. They were very well treated by Isma'il Pasha, khedive of Egypt, who offered them a three weeks’ cruise on the Nile and put at their disposal a translator, all on his expenses. Before they left Egypt, Isma'il Pasha gave Kretzulescu a sarcophagus with an Egyptian mummy, which according to a description made by French Egyptologist Auguste Marriete, belonged to Bes-An, priest of Ammon from Thebes and dated from the 16th century BC. Back in Bucharest, Kretzulescu invited prince Carol of Hohenzollern to see the mummy and then donated it to the National Museum of Antiquities.

3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.name: Palette
388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.author: Marina Minozzi
388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver
388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.description2: The cosmetic palette in slate is fish-shaped, as are many other objects found in both men and women’s graves in Egypt. It is linked to the practice of painting bodies with colours, probably for magical belief. The palette comes from a tomb excavated by David Randall-MacIver in 1902, who subsequently donated it to the Pigorini Museum in Rome. Along with the palette were found three clay scale models of ships. As a result of the excavations by W. Petrie and J. De Morgan, who documented the existence of an era preceding the 1st dynasty, Luigi Pigorini, director of the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano" decided to increase the Egyptian archaeological collection. In 1878 he began to acquire important groups, but the main body of the collection was donated by Randall-MacIver in 1901, after the excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. Another major purchase — from the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin — followed in 1905. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.

388c8605-7211-5829-b5d8-9e4bc739a3af.description: A photograph taken in 1920 showing the installation of a new telegraph pole and wiring in order to extend the telephone network that had been installed in Tangier since 1883.

39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.keywords: Egyptomania; scientific expedition; Vittorio Emanuele III; Florence; university; collection languages; Arabic; Cairo; Thebes; Luxor; Deir el-Medina; Egyptology; Nubia; hieroglyph; papyrus; papyrology; epigraphy; ostrakon; Nefertari; Ramesses II; Kha

39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.third_name: Valle delle Regine, tomba del principe Khaemuaset al momento della scoperta
39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.description2: Francesco Ballerini was an archaeologist and a curator of the Egyptian Museum in Turin. He worked at the 1902 Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt led by Ernesto Schiaparelli. He also took part in four other excavations including the tombs of Khaemuaset (No. 44) and Sethherkhepeshef (No. 43), both sons of the Pharaoh Rameses III (1183–1152 BC). The tombs were found cluttered with wooden sarcophagi and mummies dating back to a period between the 22nd-25th dynasties, as the picture shows. Both tombs had been robbed previously and showed the pink granite sarcophagi already opened and empty. In the background the viewer can see the scene of the triumph of Osiris, God of the Afterworld. The God is flanked by two funeral genii, guardians of the gates to the afterworld.

39965ec4-de1b-54df-b13b-6f3de0ef242b.name: Morse transmitter
39965ec4-de1b-54df-b13b-6f3de0ef242b.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
39965ec4-de1b-54df-b13b-6f3de0ef242b.description2: In 1840, the Ministry of Post made an announcement describing the postal service, declaring it necessary in order to facilitate communication among people. The first regulations about the postal organisation were taken from French Law in 1840. Ottoman Postal Code included 44 specific headlines. In 1855 the first telegraph service and in 1909 the first telephone service were put into common use as a demonstration of modern communication. In order to improve the technology of the telegraph systems, Ottoman authorities imported well-known machines with trademarks such as Siemens & Halske and Western Electric. As a result of this technological improvement, Ottoman officials decided to establish a telegraph factory. Between 1869 and 1915, this factory produced many devices and accessories.

3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.name: *Chateaubriand at the ruins of Carthage*
3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.archival: Chateaubriand, François-René, *Itinéraire de Paris à Jérusalem*, Tours, 1876.
3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.description2: This engraving of the French poet René de Chateaubriand shows him sitting on a hill facing the sea, surrounded by the ruins of Carthage. Fascinated by Didon's city and its glorious past, the poet visited Carthage in January 1807, and recorded his observations in his book entitled *Itinéraire de Paris à Jérusalem et de Jérusalem à Paris en Allant par la Grèce, en Revenant par l’Egypte*, published in Paris in 1811 by Lenormant, in three volumes.

3b3c9b35-91d8-5460-af41-e16d0268e789.name: Orient Express Poster
3b3c9b35-91d8-5460-af41-e16d0268e789.description2: The Orient Express, owned by the Wagon-Lits Company, connected Paris and Istanbul between 1883 and 1977. French, German, Austrian and Ottoman diplomats and civil servants were on board for its first journey. In the early years, the travellers stayed in different hotels in Istanbul but starting from 1895, passengers stayed exclusively in Pera Palace, which was bought by the Wagon-Lits Company. The Orient Express did not run during World War I, from 1914 to 1918.

3bc9a9b0-a7fe-59d9-9819-5e3a9265f4a4.name: Egyptianising necklace
3bc9a9b0-a7fe-59d9-9819-5e3a9265f4a4.description2: Gold fringe necklace in the  form of cast alternating lotus flowers and buds. Illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on 19th French jewellery. As was typical, this necklace is not derived from an original, but a more free creation based on patrern books.

3d995cca-af40-5f9f-8f23-5a077ea46883.name: Royal Decree to establish the post of *Makhzen*
3d995cca-af40-5f9f-8f23-5a077ea46883.description: The Royal Decree (dated 22 November 1892) of Mulay al-Hasan I asserted his *Makhzen* (royal authority) in order to take official control of the national post and transport services. In most localities, employees of this office were *‘Umana*, government officials, assisted by distributors.
3d995cca-af40-5f9f-8f23-5a077ea46883.keywords: Postal service; post offices; Moroccan postal service; communication; routes; port; rakkas; delivery; local postal service; foreign companies; private firms; postal network

3e275eb6-4df9-58d4-9e6a-6769cd0b3ad8.description2: Photograph showing workers at the 1904 German archaeological excavations in the area of Abusir.

3e423cff-0065-54f2-9ad6-2060de93303b.name: Barometer
3e423cff-0065-54f2-9ad6-2060de93303b.keywords: architecture; railways; Sirkeci Train Station; Anatolian Railway
3e423cff-0065-54f2-9ad6-2060de93303b.description2: This barometer was a fixture of the Ottoman Anatolian Railway Company (CFOA – Chemin de fer Otoman d'Anatolie), 19th century.

3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.name: Musée Archéologique de Sfax
3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.author: Bechir Yazidi
3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.history: Sfax, a port city in the east of the country, is Tunisia's economic centre and second city. Its town hall was built in the early 20th century, between 1905 and 1906. The builders and architects who oversaw its construction were largely Sicilian Italians and Tunisians. The town hall, built in an Arab architectural style, houses an archaeological museum on its ground floor which displayed mosaics and other Roman artefacts discovered in the ruins of Thyna.
3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.description2: Located in the centre of the new town, Sfax's town hall is topped by a gored dome and overlooked by an elegant minaret with huge clocks mounted on its walls. It was built by the firm J. B. Pace under the supervision of the architect Guy. A section of the building was transformed into an archaeological museum. Today, the museum's collection covers every period of Tunisian history. It is divided between two floors and comes mostly from ancient Taparura, with contributions from the neighbouring archaeological sites at Skhira, Acholla, Tyna and some others. The collection includes many Roman mosaics, as well as ceramics, glasswork, coins and more from the Islamic era.

3f4c6fa9-1eb4-5cf8-b351-d019a0e81489.name: Robert Hamilton Lang
3f4c6fa9-1eb4-5cf8-b351-d019a0e81489.description2: Lang was manager of the Imperial Ottoman Bank in Larnaka, 1863–1872, that ran the finances of the Ottoman administration. He conducted excavations at Dali (ancient Idlaion) in the centre of the island in the late 1860s. His report is the first systematic account of an excavation produced on the island. Lang went on to a series of posts with the IOB in Alexandria, Romania and Constantinople, becoming Director General of the bank. He was honoured by Queen Victoria, the king of Rumania, the Khedive and the Sultan.

3f842425-2ace-59ff-ad9e-176b0b58c8f7.name: *Société les Affréteurs Réunis* \[…\] *Weekly, individual direct services from Rouen and Bordeaux-Bayonne to Algeria and Tunisia, and vice versa.*
3f842425-2ace-59ff-ad9e-176b0b58c8f7.description2: In Algeria and Tunisia, the French colonisers developed viticulture, cereal farming, and the extraction of minerals for export to France. The transportation of these goods took place by boat. Various firms emerged specifically for the transportation of this type of product, providing specialised ships and regular shipments between North Africa and the major French Atlantic ports. This map indicates the ports in Tunisia and Algeria and the railway networks connecting them (Oranais network, etc.).

41c0d246-c999-5ff4-8002-64210176e2eb.name: An old exhibition from Tiled Kiosk
41c0d246-c999-5ff4-8002-64210176e2eb.dates: The Tiled Kiosk: 15th century; The photograph: 19th century
41c0d246-c999-5ff4-8002-64210176e2eb.description2: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace that dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its proximity as well as those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.

41f94376-0122-5f5e-ba32-dbcad66db68a.name: Watercolour by Claude R. Conder
41f94376-0122-5f5e-ba32-dbcad66db68a.description2: Watercolour by Claude R. Conder, made during the Survey of Western Palestine, showing one of the members of the SWP at work with one of the expedition’s theodolites. The technology they used was the latest cutting edge equipment and techniques available to the Royal Engineers, far in advance on what was being used, for example, by the US Army Corps of Engineers of the day, as was demonstrated when Lieut. Steever, of the Corps of Engineers carried out a similar survey in Transjordan.

423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.name: *Pedestal of the Obelisk in the Ancient Byzatine Hippodrome*
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.keywords: Istanbul photography; Byzantine and Ottoman architecture
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.description2: A frequently employed device in Robertson's Istanbul photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. There were two main reasons for the inclusion of these figures. For one thing, the artist used them as a way of creating a more natural scene. The other was to provide one or more reference points so that the photograph’s viewers could get an idea of the dimensions of the scene they were looking at and of the elements contained therein.

42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.name: The excavation of Mount Nemrut
42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.archival: *Le tumulus de Nemroud-Dagh. Voyage, description, inscriptions avec plans et photographies*, İstanbul, F. Loeffler, 1883.
42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters; archaeological excavations
42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.

4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.name: Rumelia Railway
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

44156a31-6bfc-5a44-9e81-6e02ec39aee7.name: Jacket
44156a31-6bfc-5a44-9e81-6e02ec39aee7.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
44156a31-6bfc-5a44-9e81-6e02ec39aee7.description2: This short men's jacket is embroidered on the two front panels, with a decoration consisting of curls, all ending in a hook shape and bordered by a floral motif emerging from a stylised vase. The open, elbow-length sleeves are decorated with geometric motifs. The sleeves are secured by small, mother-of-pearl buttons. This formal jacket was worn for important ceremonies.
