454ea471-63b6-545e-9c35-ea8207b4746b.description: View of the Erecteion in Athens. The drawing is part of the documentation of different monuments during the trip in the Arapiles frigate to Near East.
454ea471-63b6-545e-9c35-ea8207b4746b.keywords: Exploration; Early European collection; Travelling; Greece

47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.name: Materials found in the Kamiros excavations in Rodi
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.author: Marina Minozzi
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.keywords: Paleoethnology; exploration; ethnography; anthropology; material culture; collection; collector; academy; Rhodes; Cretes; Cyrene; Gortyna; Haghia Triada; Italian archaeologists in Greece; Italian archaeological school; Athens; tomb; Federico Halbherr
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.third_name: Materiali provenienti dagli scavi di Kamiros a Rodi
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.description2: Total view of materials chosen by Luigi Pernier, director of Archaeological School of Athens, from the excavation in Kamiros area (Rhodes) in 1912. Pernier sent his student Gian Giacomo Porro to the isle of Rhodes in order to explore this area and find a number of archaeological sites for the Italian Mission to concentrate its future excavations. Pernier decided to send part of the findings to the Prehistoric and Ethnographic Museum in Rome founded by Luigi Pigorini. These materials include mainly grave goods.

en: Mangani, E., “Materiali micenei, geometrici e orientalizzanti di Rodi”, in *Bullettino di Paletnologia Italiana*, Rome: Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato (2005–2007), 96, N.S. XIV: 203–310.

47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.name: *Arab Vase*
47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.description: Drawing of a vase known as "The Alhambra vase". The ceramic vase is a good example of the development of the Nasrid workshops. This vase came from the church of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción in Hornos (Jaén) and it was acquired by the National Museum of Archaeology in 1875. This type of vase is very rare and few of them have survived.
47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.artist: Drawing by Francisco Contreras; chromolithograph: Mariano Fuster
47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.keywords: Spanish Muslim art; applied arts; Alhambra
47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.third_name: *Jarrón Árabe recientemente adquirido por el Museo*

477e3472-eb64-5968-9da0-4243b0453c73.name: *The Great Hall of the Musée Assyrien in the Louvre*
477e3472-eb64-5968-9da0-4243b0453c73.second_name: Taken from the collection *Topographie de Paris*, "1er arrondissement, 1er quartier, Le Louvre"
477e3472-eb64-5968-9da0-4243b0453c73.description2: In May 1847, the world's first " Musée Assyrien" was opened at the Louvre. This was enabled by the arrival of 37 enormous bas-reliefs discovered by Paul-Émile Botta (1802–1870), the French consul in Mosul, at the site of Khorsabad. Botta, a diplomat, doctor, explorer and archaeologist, organised excavations in the hope of rediscovering Nineveh and its Assyrian monuments, and thus brought about the discovery of Khorsabad which in turn aided and accelerated the deciphering of Cuneiform in Mesopotamia. The "Musée Assyrien" pictured here was a great success and  attracted much attention on its opening in Paris in 1847.

47fcbd3c-bf49-59d2-b9ac-7634939dbb18.name: Islamic pottery from Ephesus
47fcbd3c-bf49-59d2-b9ac-7634939dbb18.description2: Excavated by John Turtle Wood, an architect and surveyor. He was employed by the Ottoman Railway Company from 1858. Between 1863–1874 he excavated on behalf of the British Museum at ancient Ephesus, where he discovered the Temple of Artemis.

481ac567-31d6-55e0-ae01-02dc70f44740.name: Archaeological excavations
481ac567-31d6-55e0-ae01-02dc70f44740.description2: General view of the Step Pyramid of Djoser in the area of Saqqara, taken at the beginning of the excavation, photo taken by Borchardt.

49ebcfec-7199-5c0b-94f3-8ed498d743df.name: Archaeological excavations
49ebcfec-7199-5c0b-94f3-8ed498d743df.description2: This picture shows workers excavating the archaeological site of Abusir in the year 1901. It documents the discovery of some archaeological pieces and columns. Photo taken by the German archaeological mission.

49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.name: Frith photograph
49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.description2: Francis Frith was one of the most successful commercial photographers from the 1850s and 1860s. He also established what was to become the largest photographic printing business in England. This image is part of the V&A's Francis Frith 'Universal Series' archive which consists of over 4000 whole-plate albumen prints predominantly of historical and topographical sites. Images such as these were highly desirable throughout the 1850s and 1860s. Frith's growing business coincided with many technological developments taking place within the field of photography. These developments changed and expanded the audience for photography and Frith's operation was well-prepared to provide for it and, it can be argued, worked to develop it employing a diverse range of publishing channels.

4acd8717-82fe-538c-b4c9-53b16ce962bb.name: The plan of Haydarpaşa Train Station
4acd8717-82fe-538c-b4c9-53b16ce962bb.description2: The original plan of Haydarpaşa Train Station, viewed from northern frontage. In 1871 Sultan Abdülaziz ordered a rail line to be built from Haydarpaşa to İzmit. Haydarpaşa station opened in 1872, and in 1888 the Anatolian Railway (CFOA) took over the line and the station. Since the station was built next to the Bosporus, freight trains would unload at Haydarpaşa and the freight would be transferred to ships. Haydarpaşa was chosen to be the northern terminus of the Baghdad Railway and the Hijaz Railway in 1904 and with rail traffic increasing, a new and larger building was required. The Anatolian Railway hired two German architects, Otto Ritter and Helmut Conu, to build the new building. They chose a neo-classical structure and construction started in 1906.

4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.name: Stele of King Nabonidus
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.type: Arched stele of Mesopotamian type with cuneiform inscription
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities, Antiquities and Museums Sector, Museum of Archaeology and Ethnography
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.dimensions: Height: 60 cm, Width: 58.5 cm, Depth/Thickness: 13 cm
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.provenance: Accumulation of debris east of a former temple building
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.author: Jamal S. Omar
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.keywords: Stele; Northwestern Arabia; archaeology; Arabian peninsula; Mesopotamia; Babylonia; cuneiform
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.description2: Upper part of a stele (once approx. 1.3 m high) with the carved representation of a standing royal figure looking towards right in front of a panel with a cuneiform inscription. Above, there are three symbols of Mesopotamian astral gods (moon disc / crescent for the moon god Sîn, the winged sun for the sun god Shamash, the star for the goddess of love and war, Ishtar). Style of the representation and text are Late Babylonian, and although the name is not preserved, the object can be attributed to the last king of Babylon, Nabû-na’id, who, for ten years, stayed at Tayma, when trying to establish control over Northwest Arabia, most probably because of economic reasons, i.e. his interest in the Arabian long distance trade. The preserved part of the inscription, however, reports on activities in his hometown Babylon.

4b13575d-f82b-573f-aa7d-a0ee196d3874.name: Archaeological excavations
4b13575d-f82b-573f-aa7d-a0ee196d3874.description2: General view of the site of the archaeological excavations in the area of Abusir. The workers' tents and those of the researchers can be observed in front of one of the pyramids of Abusir. The photo dates to 1904.

4b5af6a4-7de4-5e18-87de-8bf5e62763db.name: Dish
4b5af6a4-7de4-5e18-87de-8bf5e62763db.description: The Orientalism or Neo-Mudéjar style gave new light to old techniques such as ceramic with lustre decoration; the Manises workshops begun again to use lustre decorations and shapes from the Middle Age period.
4b5af6a4-7de4-5e18-87de-8bf5e62763db.author: Manuel Alonso

4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.name: Archaeological and topographic map of the Carthaginian ruins
4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.keywords: Phoenician, punic, roman ruins; archaeological excavations; Tunisia
4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.description2: Having been invaded and destroyed many times, the city of Carthage was then subject to various sackings, and its ruins served as a quarry for nearby towns. The site was rediscovered in the 19th century and became fashionable following the publication of Flaubert's novel *Salammbô*. Archaeologists soon felt the need for the different sites to be mapped, and in 1833 a Danish marine, Falbe, put forward a proposal for the *Recherches sur l'Emplacement de Carthage*. Thanks to the maps drawn up by the army's geographical service and military engineers, by the end of the 19th century archaeologists were able to conduct more detailed work, particularly with regards to the division of land.

4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.name: Map of the Network of Caravans
4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.keywords: Egypt; North Eastern Africa; Western Arabia; Caravans
4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.description2: This sketch shows the network of caravans in Egypt, North Eastern Africa and Western Arabia.

4e167204-1a3f-5a86-944d-ab0b42f8681b.name: Parthian Monument: the adoption of the Emperors
4e167204-1a3f-5a86-944d-ab0b42f8681b.description: During his reign, the Emperor Hadrian (figure right) adopted Antoninus Pius (centre left), who in turn adopted the 17-year-old Marcus Aurelius (left) and the eight-year-old Lucius Verus. A head stares from behind Hadrian’s left shoulder, presumably representing the guardian spirit of Aelius Verus, late father of Lucius. A bull is being offered to the gods as a sacrifice.

4ec3aa30-6ba0-5917-9e79-014b48d5cd78.name: *Giza – Austrian Headquarters*
4ec3aa30-6ba0-5917-9e79-014b48d5cd78.description2: Picture of the Austrian research headquarters in Giza. The German-born Egyptologist Hermann Junker became a professor at the University of Vienna in 1909. In 1911 the Austrian Academy obtained the concession for excavation in Giza. In 1912 Hermann Junker's team started to excavate tombs close to the pyramids of Giza.

4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.name: Palette
4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.author: Marina Minozzi
4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver; dealer
4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.description2: This slate palette, characterized by an unusual shape and an articulated decoration along one of the sides, was used to pulverize cosmetics. The absence of information about the context in which it was found make it difficult to propose a dating. Roberto Paribeni (later named superintendent of the antiquities of Rome and Lazio from 1928 to 1933) bought the palette in 1904 from the antique dealer Ghirghis in Quena on behalf of "Museo Preistorico ed Etnografico" in Rome. In 1878 Luigi Pigorini decided to enlarge the Egyptian archaeological collection in the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano", which he directed at the time. The main body of the collection was donated by David Randall-MacIver in 1901, from excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. In 1905 the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin offered more artifacts for purchase. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from the Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.

51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.name: Tramway
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.description2: This railway carraige from the French Bône-Guelma company inaugurated, in April 1879, the opening of the first section of a 100 km long line which connected Tunis to Algeria. In 1800 it also acquired the Tuni-Sousse and Tunis-Bizerte lines, and thus gained a monopoly over the construction of railway lines in Tunisia, while the Italians bought the small Tunis-La Goulette-La Marsa (TGM) railway track.

51c01d82-0b4a-5399-8607-c519021252c0.name: Switchboard (*Telefon Santrali*)
51c01d82-0b4a-5399-8607-c519021252c0.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
51c01d82-0b4a-5399-8607-c519021252c0.description2: In 1840, the Ministry of Post made an announcement describing the postal service, declaring it necessary in order to facilitate communication among people. The first regulations about the postal organisation were taken from French Law in 1840. Ottoman Postal Code included 44 specific headlines. In 1855 the first telegraph service and in 1909 the first telephone service were put into common use as a demonstration of modern communication. In order to improve the technology of the telegraph systems, Ottoman authorities imported well-known machines with trademarks such as Siemens & Halske and Western Electric. As a result of this technological improvement, Ottoman officials decided to establish a telegraph factory. Between 1869 and 1915 this factory produced many devices and accessories.

51d89765-459f-5a2f-89bb-b09f35a3e9d2.name: Firman issued by Sultan Abdülmecid for the construction of the Constanţa–Cernavodă railway
51d89765-459f-5a2f-89bb-b09f35a3e9d2.description2: The first railway in the European part of the Ottoman Empire was built in Dobruja. Its construction was leased by the Ottoman sultan to the British company "Danube and Black Sea Railway and Kustendge harbour". According to the contract signed on 1 September 1857 the company had to build a railway linking the cities Constanţa and Cernavodă and could exploit it for 99 years, after which it became property of the Ottoman Empire. The railway, inaugurated on 4 October 1860, was 66 km long and was destined for freight transportation. After Dobruja was annexed by Romania in 1878, the state bought the railway from the British company (1882). Later, in order to connect it to the Romanian railway system (since Dobruja is separated from the rest of Romania by the Danube) a railway bridge was built across the Danube.

52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.name: *The Virgin at the Nile*
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.author: Marina Minozzi
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.keywords: Egyptomania; Orientalism; painting; Orientalist paintings; artistic exchange; Egyptology; archaeology; imaginary trips; reinvention; historical events in painting; exoticism; architectural trends in painting; Italian painters; travel
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.description2: Federico Faruffini made his debut as a painter at the 1856 annual exposition of Brera. In his works the artist breaks away from the academic rule of ‘disegno’, or artistic drawing, and focuses on colour. The painting *The Virgin at the Nile* shows a sacrifice. Numerous study sketches survive. They attest that the artist was well educated on customs, traditions and architecture of ancient Egypt. In the painting the artist proposes the integration of two separate themes through different rendering styles: on the brighter upper part he sets the historic characters and in the lower zone the more narrative one, of obvious academic inspiration. The painting was brought to Paris by the artist after he decided to leave Italy because he was having difficulty finding work. After the artist committed suicide, *The Virgin at the Nile* was on display at the retrospective exhibition in Rome in 1883 where Faruffini’s entire portfolio was reconsidered, and the painting was declared his undiscussed masterpiece.

5381cedb-dcaf-5b98-864b-12a4d739c029.name: State Bank of Morocco
5381cedb-dcaf-5b98-864b-12a4d739c029.history: Establishment of the State Bank of Morocco came about through an Act signed on 7 April 1906 at the Algeciras Conference by delegates from 12 European countries, the United States and Morocco. The bank was incorporated in February 1907 as a public limited company whose registered office was in Tangiers. Its capital was divided between the signatory countries, except the United States.
5381cedb-dcaf-5b98-864b-12a4d739c029.keywords: Economy; trade; banks; banking; financing; money; Europeans in Morocco; Andalusian architecture; Arab architecture; Islamic architecture; city; urban space; changes in urban space; European style banks; European economy; European financing
5381cedb-dcaf-5b98-864b-12a4d739c029.description2: After the State Bank of Tangier was built, the Moroccan state set up a network of banks and subsequently moved the headquarters of the Central Bank to Rabat. The buildings for this banking network were built in a similar Arab-Andalusian style, in most cases in sandstone.

5441d082-5cb2-51aa-a412-66acc0afe4b5.name: Diadem
5441d082-5cb2-51aa-a412-66acc0afe4b5.description: Joaquin Sorolla travelled with his family to Tetouan in February 1919; there they bought all types of souvenirs of that exotic lands. Thanks to this travel the Sorolla Museum keep a small collection of Berber jewellery. Among the highlights is this headband or diadem, jewellery that represents the typical combination of silver and multiple enamel colours. It would look placed on the front of a woman and is complemented with bracelets, earrings, pins and necklaces, of which the Museum has also other pieces.
5441d082-5cb2-51aa-a412-66acc0afe4b5.author: Covadonga Pitarch

British ships passed through the Suez Canal on their way to India and to other British colonial possessions.

55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.author: Giulia Barrera
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.third_name: Carta della Tunisia protettorato francese, 1906 disegnata dal prof Cesidio Bonanni
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.description2: The green rectangles on the map indicate Italian agricultural settlements; the number of settlers is indicated as well. In 1906 the majority of the Italian peasants had settled around Tunis and the Gulf of Hammamet. By contrast, few Italian peasants had settled in the South and in the interior of the country (the map indicated only 300 Italian peasants near Sfax and 400 near Kef).

554cc278-49e0-58cd-8147-15ce5f2c7002.name: Lady Layard’s jewellery
554cc278-49e0-58cd-8147-15ce5f2c7002.description2: Layard, excavator of Nineveh and other sites, had this necklace made as a wedding present for his wife. It combines ancient cylinder seals in contemporary gold settings. Said to have been much admired during dinner with Queen Victoria in 1873.

56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.name: Umm Qays
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.dates: Greco-Roman until present; visited by Ulrich Seetzen in 1806
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.author: Mohammad Najjar
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.history: Founded during the 3rd century BCE, Gadara was taken first by the Seleucids of Syria during the 2nd century BCE, then by the Hasmoneans and finally “liberated” in 64 BCE by the Romans. In 30 BCE, it changed hands again to become under Herod the Great, but not for long. After the death of Herod, Gadara became part of the Roman Province of Syria. From the 4th till the 7th century, Gadara was a bishopric seat. After the battle of Yarmuk in 636, Gadara became part of the Islamic state. The most famous monuments of Gadara are its city walls and gates, theatres, octagonal basilicas and Mausoleum.
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.keywords: Province of Arabia; Roman Province of Syria; bishopric seat; battle of Yarmuk
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.description2: Located at the northern tip of Jordan, much of the Roman old city of Gadara is still covered by the deserted late Ottoman village of Umm Qays. Founded during the 3rd century BCE, Gadara was taken first by the Seleucids of Syria during the 2nd century BCE, then by the Hasmoneans and finally “liberated” in 64 BCE by the Romans. In 30 BCE, it changed hands again to become under Herod the Great, but not for long. After the death of Herod, Gadara became part of the Roman Province of Syria. From the 4th till the 7th century, Gadara was a bishopric seat. After the battle of Yarmuk in 636, Gadara became part of the Islamic state. The most famous monuments of Gadara are its city walls and gates, theatres, octagonal basilicas and Mausoleum.

574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.name: *Excavation of the Great Temple of Ramesses II at Abu Simbel*
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.description2:
An intrepid and versatile Frenchman, Linant came to Egypt in 1818. In Cairo he adopted the life of an Ottoman Turk, but was known and consulted by European residents and visitors as well as by the Pasha of Egypt, Muhammad Ali. At various times his talents were employed as a geographer, explorer, engineer, cartographer and draughtsman.  
His first adventure was an expedition to Upper Egypt that Henry Salt, British Consul-General in Egypt , took to Abu Simbel in 1818-19. Although there were other artists in the party it is likely that this watercolour is by Linant and that it depicts Salt's attempts to clear away the ever encroaching sand from the facade of the Great Temple. Linant took part in several subsequent expeditions up the Nile, and was one of the first Europeans to reach the Pharaonic sites of Meroe and Musawarat.

5838c354-7008-5b83-99dc-80cbba207468.description2: Plate with Egyptianising motifs and a copy of a drawing by Dominique Vivant Denon, *Voyage dans la Basse et la Haute Egypte, pendant les campagnes du Général Bonaparte*, 1802. 5838d2ce-d94c-553a-ba3e-9f697d70d8a3.name: Photograph of Tell el-Hesi diggers
5838d2ce-d94c-553a-ba3e-9f697d70d8a3.description2: Some members of F.J. Bliss’ workforce at Tell el-Hesi. What is most noteworthy here is that in the period up to 1938 men, women, and children all worked together on excavations.

583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.name: Archaeological Museum of the American University of Beirut
583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne, Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.history: The museum was founded in 1868 after Luigi Palma di Cesnola gifted a collection of Cypriot pottery to the newly formed American University of Beirut. Georges Post was the first curator of this collection and Morris Jesup donated the funds to construct the Post Hall which opened in 1902. The museum kept receiving collection from all around the Middle-East until 1938, after which it closed for the duration of World War II. The museum re-opened in 1948 and expanded by doubling its floor space with a refurbishment under curator D. C. Baramki which became accessible to the public in 1964. Later, in 2006, the building underwent another complete renovation under the present director, Dr. Leila Badre.
583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.keywords: museum; archaeology; exhibition; exploration; research; excavation; Museum; AUB; Archaeological; Beirut; Artefacts; Collection
583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.description2: The Archaeological Museum of the American University of Beirut is the third oldest museum in the Middle East after those in Cairo and Istanbul. The museum collections are organized in chronological order on one side and by themes on the other. The chronological displays are set along the  walls of the gallery, showing the evolution of pottery from the Chalcolitic Age (4000 BC) to the Islamic period (19th century AD). As for the thematic displays, they include the Cesnola collection, the Pre-Historic Section, the Ksar Akil excavation, the Paleolithic and Neolithic Periods, the Terracotta and Metal Figurines, the Bronze and Iron Ages, the Phoenician Civilisations, the Classical, Graeco-Roman and Byzantine and Islamic periods.

5959e6d7-d24c-578d-ae73-38a0dfc8b00d.name: *Mostaganem*
5959e6d7-d24c-578d-ae73-38a0dfc8b00d.archival: Ravoisié, A., *Exploration scientifique de l'Algérie pendant les annéees 1840-1841-1842*, vol. I, Paris: 1846.

59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.name: National Museum of Soares dos Reis
59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.history: The Carrancas Palace is a neo-classical palace built by the Moraes e Castro family, which accommodated the English generals during the Napoleonic Invasions, and was later converted into a royal residence. The National Museum of Soares dos Reis, established by King Pedro IV in 1833, was Portugal’s first public museum and was inspired by the cultural and heritage protecting spirit typical of Liberalism.
59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.keywords: Neoclassicism; Oporto; Palace; Museum; History of Art
59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.description2:
The Carrancas Palace is an imposing neoclassical building with four main areas: the U-shaped noble area, the galleries, the closed central courtyard and the backyard. Despite having been converted into a museum, the palace has preserved most of its original structure.  
The building interior has a refined decoration, shown in the stuccoes embellishing the dining room and the furniture in the music room, both of which were inspired on the creations of Robert Adams.

598fbe2f-0ba0-5a5a-92b7-3f83e20bded7.name: *Mr Drovetti and his entourage measuring a fragment of the Colossus in Upper Egypt*
598fbe2f-0ba0-5a5a-92b7-3f83e20bded7.second_name: Taken from *Voyage dans le Levant en 1817 et 1818*, by M. le Comte de Forbin
598fbe2f-0ba0-5a5a-92b7-3f83e20bded7.description2: Bernardino Drovetti (1776–1852) an Italian who joined the French army, was made a diplomat after having elicited Napoléon I's sympathy by saving his step-brother. Having been sent to Egypt as a consul, he then collected antiquities and thus portrayed himself as a defender of discovered treasures. He is pictured here with his team holding a plumb line in front of a colossus. Jean-Jacques Rifaud is leaning on the sculpture's head and dressed in an imitation of the local style. Dovretti later sold his collections to the Prince of Piedmont, to King Charles X of France and to the King of Prussia.

59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.name: Bakırköy Railway Station
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph The Hijaz Railways
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

59da1fe4-84c5-5f28-93ff-51acc78bc1c4.name: *Young Algerian man*
59da1fe4-84c5-5f28-93ff-51acc78bc1c4.description2: Much of what was written about life in Algiers during the 18th and 19th centuries focussed on the elegance of male dress. This lithographic illustrated page is taken from a collection entitled *Costumes Nationaux* which was published simultaneously in both London and Paris. It shows a young Algerian man, wearing a red *chechia* with a blue tassel, a large *sarouel* tied at the waist by a long cotton belt, and a long-sleeved embroidered *ghlila*. He is leaning on a *skemla* with a nargile pipe on top. However, even in this image the model does not have a very Algerian appearance. This was a common occurrence, as European artists would complete their works in their studios after having returned from their travels.

59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.name: Hydrographic map of Lower Egypt and part of the Suez isthmus, engraved at the Dépôt de la Guerre
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.artist: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.second_name: Drawn according to the work of M. Linant de Bellefonds, reviewed and completed in 1882 for the railways and the Suez canal. 1:250,000
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.description2: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds (1798–1883), artist and explorer passionate about Egypt, played a key role alongside Ferdinand de Lesseps in drawing and constructing the Suez Canal. He was given the title 'Bey' by the Egyptian viceroy, appointed director of Egyptian public works, and contributed to the irrigation of farmland. The map drawn in 1855 included the barriers; the outline of the Suez Canal and the railways were added in 1882.

5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.name: Official Bulletin establishing the Post, Telegraph and Telephone Office (PTT.)
5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.description: An Official Bulletin, signed by the Sultan of Morocco Mulay Yusuf ibn al-Hasan I, which concerns the creation of the Post, Telegraph and Telephone Office. The establishment of this Office was part of an agreement between Morocco and the French authorities, to promote the telecommunications sector, and put a stop to attempts by Britain and Spain to capitalise from it. The text defined the functions and services of the Office and its organisation. After independence, the Office became the Ministry (*Makhzen*) of Post, Telegraph and Telephone.

5bd17908-448f-5c04-945f-101115486457.name: Oil Painting
5bd17908-448f-5c04-945f-101115486457.description2: Large scale (over 2m long) oil painting by George Scharf of Assyrian sculpture from Nimrud, based on the original drawing by Layard.

5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.name: Map of caravan routes
5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.archival: *The Geography of Africa*, London, Gill & Sons (publisher), 1897, p. 200
5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.keywords: Route; trade; pilgrimage; pilgrims; Muslim pilgrimage; Islam; Africa; religion; economy; Holy Places; Holy Cities; Hijaz; Makka; al-Madina; Jidda; Arab Peninsula
5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.description2: This map illustrates the trading caravan routes crossing the Sahara desert from Mediterranean ports (Tripoli, Tafilet, Tunis, Algiers and Oran) to sub-Saharan cities. The trading routes were connected north and south to three pilgrim routes for Mecca. The northern pilgrim route from Tunis and Tripoli included Siwah, Cairo, Suez and Aqaba. From Aqaba, meeting the pilgrim route from Damascus, it continued along the coast of Arabia to Mecca. The central route continued from Siwah through the oases of Dakkel and El-Kharjeh to ports on the Red Sea to Jeddah and Mecca. The southern route followed the valley of the Upper Niger through Timbuctu, Gao, Sokoto, Kano, Lake Chad and Kordofan to the port of Swakin on the Red Sea and continued to Jeddah by ship.

5d9c0ecc-1cda-5806-b890-7ae8e461a596.name: Postal stamp
5d9c0ecc-1cda-5806-b890-7ae8e461a596.description: The Moroccan Telegraph Company, which had been responsible for the national post since 1911, started issuing stamps mainly to secure mail and parcels under the name of the “Management of the Chérifienne Post, Telegraph and Telephone”. This means that the first Moroccan stamp was issued on 22 May 1912.

5e05c455-44c3-5bd3-be12-061bbab9de8d.name: Musée de Cherchell. Fragments found in the excavations.
5e05c455-44c3-5bd3-be12-061bbab9de8d.second_name: Taken from *L'Algerie Phtographiée*, vol. 2, Province d'Alger
5e05c455-44c3-5bd3-be12-061bbab9de8d.description2: The French established two museums in Algeria after the conquest: one in Algiers (1838), and another in Cherchell (1840). The latter was overshadowed by the reputation of the former and lacked subsidies. A report from 1855 describes abandoned collections, to which the objects found during an 1856 excavation were soon added. This image, dating from 1856, highlights both the richness of the works presented to the Musée de Cherchell and their inadequate conservation. A new museum, built in 1908, allowed the collections to be stored in better conditions.

5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.name: Postal map
5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.description2: The network of routes for sending messages and transporting troops and supplies was carried out with a relay system, established in the 16th century in the Ottoman Empire. The messengers, who conveyed dispatches throughout the country, were identified as the Tatars. Private or personal correspondence was not a part of that relay system; it was built to fulfil governmental needs. Because of this reason the *reaya* (public) created an alternative postal method by using caravans, pilgrims, and private couriers called *ulaks*. The *Tanzimat* Decree, which was the declaration of process included reformation, modernization and westernization in 1839, proved that the Ottoman Empire was focused on its policy of changing governing to be more like modern Western European-style administrative practices.

5f7be233-5b3b-542f-9b15-c37a25a0932f.description2: Plan of the area to the South of the Haram al-Sharif, Jerusalem, showing the location of the shafts dug by Lieut. Charles Warren, R.E., and his team to explore the topography of ancient Jerusalem. This work established the history of the development of the Old City of Jerusalem. While engaged in this work, Warren also carried out a major study of the economy of Jerusalem in the period 1867–1870, which was published in the SWP in 1884.

614be63b-02e7-5f3d-b90a-32e42c8270fa.description2: Plaster cast of a Neo-Hittite relief. The original was excavated at Carchemish by Hogarth, Woolley and Lawrence between 1911 and 1913. The originals, since damaged, are now in Ankara.

61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.name: Messageries Maritimes's Istanbul-themed posters
61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.description2: *Messageries maritimes* was a French merchant shipping company. When it began, it operated on routes to the Middle East. Its ships were used as troop transports during the Crimean War, and were so helpful for the army that the Emperor gave the company the right to operate on the Bordeaux-Brazil route as thanks. This was the first French transatlantic line equipped with steamers. The following year, the *Société générale maritime* (later called *Compagnie générale transatlantique*) received the North Atlantic lines. From 1871 to 1914 the shipping company, now called *Compagnie des messageries maritimes*, saw its Golden Age.

61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.name: *The Port of Constanţa*
61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.description2: The Black Sea port of Constanța underwent its first modernization while Dobruja, the province where it is situated, was under Ottoman control. In 1857, when the Ottoman government hired a British company to build a railway in Dobruja, the concluded contract also stipulated the reconstruction of the Constanța port. Completed in 1864, it was still a small harbor with a wooden dock, a dam and one cereals depot. After Dobruja was annexed by Romania, a law was issued in 1885 for the “improvement and augmentation” of the port. In 1896 its modernization was leased to a French enterprise but due to some disagreements, three years later the state took over the works, which were led by architect Anghel Saligny. Inaugurated in 1909, the new port had 3 dams, several docks, depots, silos, an oil basin, an electric plant.

62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.name: National Museum of Archaeology
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.author: DGPC
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.history: The National Museum of Archaeology was founded in 1893 inside the Monastery of Jerónimos, which is one of the most important testimonies to Portugal’s Great Discoveries. With 120 years of existence, the museum became a reference institution of Portuguese Archaeology having regular contacts with museums, universities and research centers across the globe.
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.keywords: Archaeology; Museum; Rediscovry the past; National Identiity
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.architects: Architects: Master Diogo Boitaca (c.1460–1527), João de Castilho (c.1470–1552), Jerónimo de Ruão (1530–1601)
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.description2: The Jerónimos Monastery is one of the most important examples of Manueline architecture. Its church, built in a lengthwise plan to the design of Boitaca, is divided into three naves topped by a flattened vault supported by eight towering octagonal pillars. This system provides a unified and luminous space. The main portal, which also gives access to the cloister, boasts a statuary programme depicting the Nativity. The church’s side portal, by João de Castilho, features sculptural images of the Virgin, the Apostles, Prophets, Doctors of the Church and angels. The museum is located in the monastery’s west wing which held the monks’ dormitories in the past.

63946b1b-16ea-516e-a633-bafee1467d3f.name: Ionian capital from the *Ptolemaion*
63946b1b-16ea-516e-a633-bafee1467d3f.description: This fragmented capital, displaying a Greek-scrolled valuta and a wealth of floriform decoration on the cushion, originates from the so-called Ptolemaion, a gateway built in Samothrace for the Egyptian king Ptolemy II Philadelphus.

6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.name: *Comic Map of Seat of War with Entirely New Features* (London: Rock Brothers and Payne, 1854)
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.author: Renata De Simone
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.archival: ASPa, Ministero per gli Affari di Sicilia, busta 1199, fasc. 212
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.second_name: A satirical map of Europe during the Crimean war
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.description2:
In the annex to the map, the authors made explicit their view on the international situation and the political message that they intended to promote. They portrayed Russia as “the Great Bear of Europe”: a tyrannical power, epitome of despotism and oppression, which used the whip against her own subjects. “The claws of the Bear, improperly extended to the Black Sea, are undergoing the process of being clipped by our brave fellows”.  
Turkey, which was participating in the war on the side of Britain, was represented as a turkey. The authors argued that it was no longer the “sick bird of Europe”. With “head erect and again in good feather”, Turkey looked “its defiance to Russia”. England was described as “the old Lion of the World, majestic, strong and patient”.

678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.name: *The Barrage or Nile dam*
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.archival: Smith, James - Minister of St. George's-in-the-West Parish, Aberdeen, *A Pilgrimage to Egypt: an account of a visit to Lower Egypt ... With ... Illustrations*, Aberdeen: J. Avery & Co., 1897, p. 261
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.keywords: Pilgrimage; Christian pilgrimage; travel; travel book; Egypt; Nile; inventions; dams; irrigation; flood; agriculture; economy; French in Egypt
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.description2: This picture, from the book *A Pilgrimage to Egypt: An Account of a Visit to Lower Egypt*, shows the Delta Barrage dam built by the French engineer Mougelle during the reign of Muhammad 'Ali Pasha to maintain the Nile water at a balanced level all the year. The barrage also served as a fortification against attack on Cairo or Upper Egypt. It consisted of a double bridge, the eastern part spanning the Damietta branch of the Nile, the western the Rosetta, with the head of the Delta between the two. The barrage had to be improved from 1883 by Sir Colin Scott Moncrief to solve structural problems with the foundations and the gates of the dam. The barrage and other dams testify to the importance of these structures to provide the water needed for irrigation in Egypt since antiquity.

6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.name: *View Looking across the Hall of Columns, Karnak*
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.description2: Roberts' viewpoint across the Great Hypostyle Hall, in the Precinct of Amon-Re, at the Temple Complex at Karnak, captures in great detail the physical features of the monument as it appeared in his day. At the same time, he used exaggerated proportions to convey the structure’s imposing scale, which impressed him deeply. In his diary he writes: ’Karnak is even more astonishing than Luxor. Its magnificence is unimaginable. Trying to describe rationally what I have seen would be ridiculous’. In the 19th century,, the Karnak temple complex became one of the most famous ancient Egyptian sites visted by artists and archaeologists. During his travels up and down the Nile, Roberts captured over 300 monuments and ruins in his unprecedentedly detailed and precise works, many of them before excavation or restoration.  In his work, Roberts also drew on the pioneering scholarship of scholars like Champollion. The final depictions subtlely contributed to the Orientalist discourse on Ancient Egypt, which Europe increasingly saw as their right to appropriate.
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium

6a89da25-5756-58bf-b49f-f4fde99fe13b.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
6a89da25-5756-58bf-b49f-f4fde99fe13b.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Archaology Museum
6a89da25-5756-58bf-b49f-f4fde99fe13b.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen had been exposed to Westernizing ideas through education and travel. This museum was founded by decree as the Imperial Museum (*İmparatorluk Müzesi*) in 1891. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi Bey. Construction of the main building began in 1881, attaining its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. The site of the museum belonged to the Topkapı Palace outer gardens. It is a prominent structure built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul.

6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.name: Map of Beirut
6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.holder: American University of Beirut, Jafet Library, Archives and Special Collections Department
6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.keywords: Expansion; Map; Districts; Consulates; Routes; City; Beirut
6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.description2: This map dates to 1876 and was drawn by the acting Danish Consul, Julius Loytved for the Sultan 'Abd al-Hamid II. Loytved was a map-maker, an archaeologist, and the director of various Anglo-Syrian schools. This detailed survey map includes 12 districts of Beirut: 1 - The Old City and the *suq*; 2 - Al-Zaytuna; 3 - Ras Beirut; 4 - Msaytbe; 5 - Mazraat al-Arab; 6 - Ras el-Naba'; 7 - Al-Bashura; 8 - Achrafieh; 9 - St. Dimitri; 10 - Mimas; 11 - Rmeil; 12 - Al-Saifi. The roads to Damascus, Saida and Tripoli are all clearly indicated by emphasis on the edge of the map. The map also indicates 47 other points of interest, including 91 consulates, military posts, government buildings, educational and health institutions, public parks, private gardens, cemeteries, archaeological sites, and sand and rock hills.

6b95b4dd-912b-59ba-93e0-00f63bedc323.name: SWP Geological Map
6b95b4dd-912b-59ba-93e0-00f63bedc323.description2: This was the first ever geological map of Palestine, drawn up in the late 1880’s by Edward Hull. It enabled, for the first time, the accurate assessment of the geological resources of the country, and potentially their exploitation to the benefit of the local economy, as well as revealing the history and structure of the landscape.

6cd69b5c-2452-5c87-b27b-fa34cce6a025.description2: This photo is from a gelatine print negative, and it was included in the archive of the archaeological area of Saqqara, Giza.

6e327e6c-97a6-5021-bdda-e534a67a0765.name: Reserve head
6e327e6c-97a6-5021-bdda-e534a67a0765.description: The *Reserve head* is one of the major works of the Viennese collection, found in an early tomb in the burial grounds of Giza. Though stylized, the visage is still full of life, with simultaneously idealized and very regular features. Scholars still disagree about the purpose of this type of object. Traditional explanations proffer their use as surrogate heads for the soul (mummifying having then been only in its earliest stages).
6e327e6c-97a6-5021-bdda-e534a67a0765.dates: 4th Dyn. c. 2600 BC; acquired by Hermann Junker during his excavation in Giza 1912–1929

6f32665b-a3e9-5152-9c94-67a17540cfed.description2: Picture of the Austrian team's Egyptian cook. In 1911 the Austrian Academy obtained the concession for excavation in Giza. In 1912 Hermann Junker's team started to excavate tombs close to the pyramids of Giza.

6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.name: Dougga archaeological site
6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.history: Dougga, which was a North African city under Roman control during the Numidian period, contains almost perfectly preserved remains of an ancient city and its different elements, and presents the best example of how indigenous cities were adapted, for better or for worse, to the Roman urban model. When the first European explorers travelled through the Regency of Tunis, the Dougga (Thugga) site attracted both theirs and the scientific community's attention more than any other ancient city. The site is remarkably preserved, and its ruins were therefore a great source of interest and fascination. This interest peaked when the Englishman Thomas Reade stole a Libyco-Punic inscription.
6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.keywords: Numidian; Roman; indigenous; temple; sanctuary; Tanit; Ba'al/Saturn
6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.description2: Located in the Teboursouk region in north-east Tunisia, this archaeological site is notable for its size - 70 hectares - its excellently preserved monuments and its rich past, having witnessed more than 15 centuries of history covering the Punic, Numidian, Roman and Byzantine eras. It contains a great variety of temples and sanctuaries, such as those dedicated to Ba'al/Saturn and to Tanit/Caelestis, a capitoline triad, a public square, a theatre, large public baths, private homes of varying wealth, funerary monuments and more. Many of these monuments were one of a kind, and so in December 1997 Dougga archaeological site was listed as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

6fb5d317-b1c7-55c6-a5a1-452d17f4b70a.name: *10 cents an issue. Le Télégraphe. Morning Newspaper. Special connections with the whole world.*
6fb5d317-b1c7-55c6-a5a1-452d17f4b70a.description2: Claude Chappe's invention of optical telegraphy was a turning point in the development of telecommunications. Built high up (e.g. on a hill or a roof), the mechanism consisted of a pole with movable arms, visible from a distance, which transmitted a code. Telegraphy became a very popular mode of communication during times of war, and was adopted by the National Convention of the First Republic in 1793. Even Napoléon I, who had shut down the French telegraph lines for fear of political troubles, had them reopened and extended to Europe in order to fight the anti-French Coalition. Telegraphy was an increasingly used mode of communication in the 19th century.

70b437a4-41c0-50dd-839c-7f248f97ae34.author: Hayet Touaibia
70b437a4-41c0-50dd-839c-7f248f97ae34.description2: In August 1840 and again in 1848 Delamare visited the ruins of Cuicul, an ancient Roman colony founded by Nerva and Trajan at the end of the first century. He brought a number of sketches back from these visits, with the most important of these currently kept at the Cabinet du Livre in the old library at the Sorbonne. This drawing, kept at the Musée des Beaux-Arts, accurately reproduces of the ruins of the theatre, built in the second century beyond the city walls.

70d49b3f-e99f-5946-83f7-c0c3b1092a69.archival: *Le tumulus de Nemroud-Dagh. Voyage, description, inscriptions avec plans et photographies*, İstanbul, F. Loeffler, 1883.

70d49b3f-e99f-5946-83f7-c0c3b1092a69.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.

736a018e-a855-56c6-a0e4-184b1dba4cd5.description: South Arabia (Yemen) has always been famous for its incense. The cultivation and widespread trade of this desirable product turned Yemen into a very important region with a highly autonomous culture. This kind of head, sculpted on tombstones, portrayed the subject partly as abstract idealization and yet in a very naturalistic way.
736a018e-a855-56c6-a0e4-184b1dba4cd5.dates: Beginning of 1st millenium AD South-Arabia; brought to Vienna by Edward Glaser in 1882–1894

737d2ad8-e855-5e34-9a89-714f0aed6dff.description2: Following the work of Champollion, decoding texts and archaeological discoveries became some of the main interests of popular science journals. 752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.name: Jerash
752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.author: Mohammad Najjar
752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.history: Jerash has a long occupational history that starts in prehistoric times and goes through various historical periods until the present. During the Greco-Roman period, Jerash was a prominent member of the Decapolis. It was part of the Islamic Empire starting from the 7th century AD. The small village of Jerash was identified by Ceetzen as the Decapolis town of Gerasa by Ulrich Jasper Ceetzen in his journey from Damascus to Jerusalem in 1806.
752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.keywords: Rediscovery; identification; Decapolis; Greco-Roman period; Seetzen
752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.description2: Jerash is probably the most famous heritage town in Jordan after Petra. It is one of the best preserved Greco-Roman provincial towns from the Roman/Byzantine period. The western part of the town was completely preserved and protected. It shows a city planned with fortification walls, gates, paved and colonnaded streets, temples, theatres, the hippodrome and many churches with mosaic floors.

78482946-b8d7-5fca-913f-fd0e2dc38b4a.description: A 19th-century map of the Moroccan Empire and the states of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli. Its toponyms are written in French. 789458d3-49a6-51d8-9be2-897051433c19.description2: A commemorative piece custom made to honour Austen Henry Layard. Layard was famous for excavating Nineveh. Closely modelled on the sculptures discovered by Layard.

79791fd6-4a63-5950-8b88-e5b802feebd3.name: Research on the location of Carthage (with 15 illustrated pages)
79791fd6-4a63-5950-8b88-e5b802feebd3.description2: Christian Théodore Falbe, captain of a Danish ship and explorer, was the Tunisian consul before becoming  delegate for the Société pour l'Exploration de Carthage. Fable dedicated himself to developing a new map of Tunis, which required the use of newly developed techniques. He had to use his cunning to be able to draw these plans, as he had aroused the suspicion of the Tunisian population, and ended up doing many of them from the roofs of neighbouring consulates. His pioneering work on Carthage should be seen as part of a greater international movement which had recently taken great interest in this destroyed and long-forgotten city.

7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.name: *Map to illustrate the Route of David Roberts Esq. R. A. in the Holy Land, Petrea and Syria*
7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.description2: This map shows the areas visited by the Scottish artist David Roberts (1796-1864) during the 11 months he spent travelling between Egypt, the Sinai, Jordan and Palestine in 1838/39. Roberts subsequently became famous for his meticulous lithographs of Egypt, the 'Holy Land' and other Near Eastern regions, hardly touched as yet by British artists at the time. Maps like this one were provided with each complete set of his lithographs later to help trace the locations Roberts visited and sketched.Roberts' depictions were to become extremely important tools in popularising the ‘Holy Land’ in 19th century British imagination, thus encouraging ever more people to visit, map and survey it. His work also helped to underpin the aspirations and objectives of the Palestinian Exploration Fund, founded in 1865.

7a241c8e-d68e-5a99-8f6d-768433eb938e.name: Map of the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia
7a241c8e-d68e-5a99-8f6d-768433eb938e.description2: This map of Lombardy-Venetia from 1827 shows postal routes and information concerning the costs of travelling with the post coaches.

7a7a871e-70a7-5428-91b9-c5c8fd581ce1.second_name: Main gate of the ancient city of Babylon, reconstruction with many original pieces
7a7a871e-70a7-5428-91b9-c5c8fd581ce1.description2: The Museum of the Ancient Near East, dating back to 1899, considers itself as a place where cultures of the region can be studied, but also as the custodian of the rich excavation finds from German field studies. The most eminent examples of the custodial work are the Processional Way and the Ishtar Gate of ancient Babylon, of whom only the foundational walls were exposed during excavations in 1902. Only after thousands of fragments had been put together, the reconstruction could be integrated into the museum.

7aeb03eb-d2c3-50a9-9ca0-0776ebf921fd.name: Sarcophagus of the mourning women
7aeb03eb-d2c3-50a9-9ca0-0776ebf921fd.dates: It is thought to be the sarcophagus of the King of Sidon, Straton (374-358 BC)
7aeb03eb-d2c3-50a9-9ca0-0776ebf921fd.keywords: Sarcophagus Sidon; The Hellenistic Period; Istanbul Archaeological Museums
7aeb03eb-d2c3-50a9-9ca0-0776ebf921fd.description2: In the Sarcophagus of the Crying Women, found at the Royal Necropolis in Sidon like the Alexander Sarcophagus, nothing could be found other than the bones of its owner and a bronze belt buckle, since it had been robbed in an earlier time. From the partial traces on the marble that remained until today, it is understood that it had been dyed in blue and red initially. It is the best example of the group called by archaeologists "Sarcophagi with Columns", and it is considered as a final resting place, like the "Mausoleum of Halicarnassus" or the "Nereid Monument", rather than a tomb. Its architectural features were used in the architecture of the old building of the İstanbul Archaeological Museums. It is an example of Greek sculpture displaying Eastern influences. The shaved heads, bare feet, ragged clothes of the figures and their movements and expressions of sadness are features of Semitic societies. It is thought to be the sarcophagus of the King of Sidon, Straton (374-358 BC), who was said to have led a life of pleasure. The sarcophagus has the shape of an Ionian temple.

7bb89a63-82a6-5695-bd9f-cf857d8d19fb.name: *Northern side of the tomb of the Christian woman. Excavations carried out by detachment of the Zouave regiments, under the direction of Berbrugger* \[curator of the *Musée d'Alger*\].
7bb89a63-82a6-5695-bd9f-cf857d8d19fb.second_name: Taken from *L'Algerie Phtographiée*, vol. 2, Province d'Alger
7bb89a63-82a6-5695-bd9f-cf857d8d19fb.description2: Adrien Berbrugger (1801–1869) was an archaeologist specialising in Algeria, who founded the first Musée d'Algérie in Algiers (1838). He visited the "tomb of the Christian woman" for the first time in 1835. This burial mound, located near Tipaza in the south of the Algerian Sahel, had misidentified as an erroneous French translation had rendered "Roman" as "Christian". Berburgger launched various archaeological campaigns which would demonstrate that it was in fact a royal mausoleum from Mauretania. in 1855, for the first time in the history of archaeological excavations, the work of archaeologists was photographed. This photograph is from a "pictorial report" created by Frère Moulin as he passed through Algiers, and shows Berbrugger (by the door), John Green (the archaeological campaign's photographer) and a dozen Zouaves who had taken part in the excavation.

7c890fcb-159c-520c-b75f-6a2a5003b92c.keywords: Campaign in Egypt; Egyptomania; archaeology; Leopoldo II; Charles X; scientific expedition; university; museums; collection; collector; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; Thebes; languages; hieroglyph; epigraphy; Orientalist; travelling artist; botany
7c890fcb-159c-520c-b75f-6a2a5003b92c.third_name: I. Rosellini, *Monumenti dell'Egitto e della Nubia*, Pisa 1832–1843: frontespizio
7c890fcb-159c-520c-b75f-6a2a5003b92c.description2: Back from the Franco-Tuscan expedition (1828-29), Francois Champollion and Ippolito Rosellini worked on publishing drawings and notes collected during the voyage in Egypt. Unfortunately Champollion died in 1831 (he was only 41 years old) and Rosellini had to carry on the huge project on his own, publishing the texts and also the atlas plates in folio. The original materials for the publication are preserved today at the University Library of Pisa.

7d30a2cd-fc11-5624-b8c4-b8d92b2e5e38.name: Photograph of Tétouan Railway Station, platform
7d30a2cd-fc11-5624-b8c4-b8d92b2e5e38.description: Completion of the railway line that connected Tétouan with Ceuta relates closely to plans for the construction of the new Port of Ceuta. This photograph depicts Tétouan Railway Station in relation to construction of the port. It was the military engineers Captain Mario Pinto and First Lieutenant Levi Arsenio Jimenez Montera who first offered to draft plans for the new line between the two cities, a distance of nearly 1,435m, and managed to get the project approved by the Ministry of War. While some railway lines in Morocco were abandoned early, this one resisted closure until the dawn of independence. Evidence shows that the route thrived during the Protectorate era as it was one of main Spanish penetration axes to the North at the time.

7eacd600-e860-593a-aed7-a9329d9d9011.name: Fragment of the Parthenon frieze
7eacd600-e860-593a-aed7-a9329d9d9011.description: The climax of the Greater Panathenaia, the chief festival of Athens, held in honour of Athena, was a procession which ended with the presentation of the newly woven *peplos* (a woman’s garment) to the tutelary goddess of the city. This is the subject of the frieze around the cella of the Parthenon, the temple on the Athenian Acropolis. This fragment depicts the garment being handed over in the presence of the goddess.

8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.artist: Photograph: author unknown; building: architect Vedat Tek, architect Muzaffer Bey
8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.description2: The Istanbul Main Post Office is an office building for postal services located at the *Sirkeci* quarter of the faith district in Istanbul, Turkey. It was designed by architect Vedat Tek in the First Turkish National architectural style and was constructed between 1903 and 1909. (Vedat Tek was a notable Turkish architect, who has been one of the leading figures of the First Turkish National Architectural Movement. He studied at the *École Centrale Paris*, graduating with a degree in civil engineering before he got his further education in architecture at the *Ecole des Beaux Arts* in Paris.) The four-story building houses a post office, the *Sirkeci* Post Office, office space for regional administration and also since 2000 the Istanbul Postal Museum. It is Turkey's largest post office building.

830c2e47-9fe7-5cca-984a-d06b95466a30.name: *Sketches of Aden*
830c2e47-9fe7-5cca-984a-d06b95466a30.description: These drawings show Steamer Point, an early British settlement in Aden, and one early steamer. *Sketches of Aden* is an account by a British officer who settled in Aden in the first half of the 19th century. Published in Madras in 1848, the book offers a synthesis of the history, geography, people and costumes of that important British settlement on the route to India. Although influenced by 19th-century European stereotypes and by the impact of a new environment, the author describes vividly the political events leading to the British conquest of the port in 1839, the ancient legends and the main events in the local history of Aden, its towns, commerce, living conditions and the heterogeneous population living in Aden: the Arab, Somali, Jewish and Indian communities.

87e70362-8746-56dc-8457-3ebaaa0bc58a.name: Ottoman map of the Romanian countries
87e70362-8746-56dc-8457-3ebaaa0bc58a.description2: This is a map of Moldavia and Wallachia dating from after 1812, when following the Russian-Ottoman war of 1806-1812 Russia annexed the Eastern part of Moldavia, thereafter called Bessarabia (which used to be the name by which southern Moldavia was known). The red line marks the new border that the peace treaty of Bucharest (1812) established between the Ottoman Empire and Russia. The light blue line marks the border between Moldavia and Wallachia, the yellow one that between Austria and the Ottoman Empire and the thick blue line represents the border between Bulgaria and Wallachia. The green line marks the frontiers of the Ottoman Empire.

898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.name: *Head of the Great Sphinx, Pyramids of Geezeh July 17th, 1839*
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.description2: Roberts depicted the Sphinx some twenty years after Giovanni Battista Caviglia had excavated at Giza in 1817 and had cleared masses of sand away from the monument, which up to that point had been buried right up to its neck. Subsequently, he succeeded in clearing the whole front of the Sphinx. At the point of Roberts’ visit, the sphinx was visible from the top of the head to the floor of the temple between its paws. After its initial discovery, the Sphinx soon became one of the foremost fascinations for early European Egyptologists, including Auguste Mariette, the founder and first director of the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, Gaston Maspero, who conducted a survey  of it in 1886, and the British scholar E. A. Wallis Budge.It also proved fascinating for Orientalist artists and artisans all over Europe. In Roberts' artwork, the stone-cut monument is rendered in great detail, carefully recording also the far-reaching damage to the Sphinx’s face, the cause of which had already given rise to much discussion and speculation at the time. The Pyramids in this view are that of Cheops, or the Great Pyramid, seen on the right, and on the left, that of Cephren, also known as the Second Pyramid.

8b5de31f-f1e0-5ddc-9d8a-dd777ed6d387.name: Mosaic for the inauguration of the Musée du Bardo
8b5de31f-f1e0-5ddc-9d8a-dd777ed6d387.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8b5de31f-f1e0-5ddc-9d8a-dd777ed6d387.description2: This mosaic was made for the inauguration of the Musée Alaoui, now the Musée du Bardo, on 7 May 1888. At the top right-hand side we can see the Tunisian flag, on the left the the initials of the French General Residence in Tunisia, and in the centre the words  "Le Musée Alaoui"  in red letters. The inauguration was hosted by 'Ali Pacha Bey and the Resident-General M. J. Massicault. The names of the French civil servants who had accompanied the Resident-General and supervised the creation of the museum are written in two colums: M. Georges Perrot and M. Edouard Delpeuch, delegates from the Ministre de l'Instruction Publique des Beaux-Arts, M. Henri Wallon and M. Héron de Villefosse, from l’Académie des Inscriptions et Belles Lettres, and M. R. de la Blanchére, director of the Service des Antiquités et des Arts. Finally, the Arabic text at the bottom of the mosaic celebrates the inauguration of the museum.

8ba03860-993b-5dbf-9a66-b44cd6b52d86.name: Simplon-Orient Express Poster
8ba03860-993b-5dbf-9a66-b44cd6b52d86.description2: Roger Broders was a French illustrator and artist best known for his travel posters promoting tourism destinations in France. Broders' illustrations were distinctive for their simple lines and bold, flat areas of colour, combined with noticeable graphical perspective showing the featured mountains and seascapes in the background. Broders' illustrations depicting people show active, elongated figures wearing elegant, contemporary clothes. His posters were simply and boldly lettered identifying the destination, and were supplemented with a brief slogan.

8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

90ac8914-3124-5940-a90b-536222104ba2.description2: The Pergamon Museum building owes its name to a spectacular finding in Turkey. The story of this discovery of the past starts in 1864 with the German engineer Carl Humann, who urged the Berlin museums to undertake proper excavations when he saw local lime burners burning ancient remains on the acropolis. The subsequent research unveiled important remains of Hellenistic art. With the museum opening in 1930 and the architectural reconstructions of the Ancient, Hellenistic, Roman and Islamic Middle East the museum developed in one of the most famous institutions of its kind.

920e1526-6e4c-5336-8f89-0cc695c54cff.description2: In 1814 Ker Porter, British artist and travelller, visited Rich. Together they explored famous sites in Iraq. He mistook the ruins at Aqar Quf for the Tower of Babel. The box contains fragments of a Babylonian mudbrick and bitumen, matching the Biblical description of the Tower.

93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.name: The Moorish Villa (Wilhelma Park)
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.description2:
The "Moorish Villa" at Wilhelma indicates either the whole construction of the botanical section or its central building. The glasshouses are impressive constructions of glass and cast iron adjoined to the central living quarters already during the reign of Wilhelm I of Württemberg.  
The overall construction accommodate five autonomous plant houses, each of them displaying plants according to a super-ordinate theme. From the northern entrance, one first reaches the Cactus Cupola House, then the room with the Tropical Crop Plants. In the centre there follows the Moorish Villa (central part of the construction), with the famous giant titan plant. The next section is the glasshouse with tropical ferns, and in the final room, also with a glass cupola, the tree ferns.  
In the central room of the Moorish Villa construction there is the Department for Nocturnal Animals with nocturnal birds.

93c53f75-811e-5d47-8d12-4f56a360451f.name: Carthage archaeological site
93c53f75-811e-5d47-8d12-4f56a360451f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
93c53f75-811e-5d47-8d12-4f56a360451f.history: Founded by the Phoenicians around 814 BC, Carthage was the city that brought Africa into mainstream European historical narratives. Hanno's Carthage ruled the seas, and Hannibal's Carthage was master of the land; Carthage certainly saw its golden age before disappearing. Augustus built Carthage as the capital of proconsular Africa, and the Imperial Roman Carthage that succeeded it put great importance on art and literature. Christian Carthage of Saint Augustine's times appeared to be a city fuelled by religion and passion. It was ruled by the Vandals for a century, then the Byzantines and finally the Arabs. However, although the leadership changed many times over the years, Carthage itself did not move. Modern Carthage, therefore, holds the evidence for many different histories. It has been listed as a UNESCO world heritage site since the 26 October 1979.

93c53f75-811e-5d47-8d12-4f56a360451f.description2: Explorers and travellers - starting with T. Falbe and E. Beulé in the early 19th century and continuing through to the end of the 20th century - have been fascinated by interrogating and analysing the remains of one of the most important ancient cities: Carthage. It was conquered by Hassan ibn Nu'man in 698, but was then abandoned by the Arab Muslim population in favour of Tunis, and so for twelve decades was used as a quarry for marble and other stone for the construction of monuments in Tunis and other cities. By the early 20th century only some of what is visible today had been uncovered, namely the baths of Antoninus with their great cisterns, the huge cisterns of La Malga, some sections of the aqueduct connecting Carthage to Zaghwan, the lagoons of the two Punic ports, the remains the amphitheatre and the perimeter of the circus.

9599bee6-4ecd-5e61-803d-f6a17fddee21.history: The Istanbul Main Post Office is an office building for postal services located at Sirkeci quarter of Fatih district in Istanbul, Turkey. It was designed by architect Vedat Tek in First Turkish National architectural style and was constructed between 1903 and 1909. The four-story building houses a post office, the Sirkeci Post Office, office space for regional administration and also since 2000 the Istanbul Postal Museum. It is Turkey's largest post office building.

96e36ed2-2da9-5b5a-b4bb-79b6897cf288.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
96e36ed2-2da9-5b5a-b4bb-79b6897cf288.description2: Ahmad Faris al-Shidyaq was born in 1804 in the 'Ashqut (Keserwan) district, and received his primary education in Hadath (Ba'abda), and his secondary education in 'Ayn Warka School. Here, he studied both foreign languages and Arabic literature. He was later converted to Protestantism by American missionaries in the region. He moved to Egypt in 1825, and then to Malta in 1834, where he lived for 14 years. During this period he became the head of the American Printing Press, and started publishing his own books. From Malta, he travelled to London, Paris and Tunis, where he converted to Islam and changed his name to Shaykh Ahmad Faris al-Shidyaq. In 1857, he began publishing his newspaper whilst he continued to edit his books. He died on 20 September 1889, and was buried in Lebanon, in Hazmiyya.

9d2ab4b5-fef1-530e-806a-e497c463b2a5.description2: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace that dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its proximity as well as those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.

It was located inside the village of the craftsmen who worked at the royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings. The holder had been "Head of the royal necropolis" and "Superintendent to the works of the royal necropolis" in the middle of the 18th dynasty, during the reigns of Amenhotep II (1428–1397 BC), Thutmose IV (1397–1388 BC) and Amenhotep III (1388–1351 BC). Considered the most beautiful monument of ancient Africa, the Amphitheatre of El Jem was listed as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO on 26 October 1979.

He chose to specialise professionally in the photography of important construction sites. Thanks to him, today we can reconstruct the building of, for example, the Marne Dam at Noisiel in 1885. This dam is associated with the famous chocolatier Menier who became a pioneer in the field of cocoa refining, introducing the use of water power, among other new methods for the refinement of cocoa.

a7d32c3d-fe87-5afb-b350-091e02c5d6d1.keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver
a7d32c3d-fe87-5afb-b350-091e02c5d6d1.description2: This ivory tooth-shaped amulet, decorated with a series of diagonal parallel lines, comes from the excavations conducted between 1900 to 1901 by David Randall-MacIver and Luigi Pigorini. As a result of earlier excavations by W. Petrie and J. De Morgan, who documented the existence of an era preceding the 1st dynasty, Pigorini, an archaeologist and the director of the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano", decided to increase the museum’s Egyptian archaeological collection. In 1878 he began to acquire important groups, but the main body of the collection was donated by Randall-MacIver in 1901, from excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. Another major purchase — from the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin — followed in 1905.  The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.

en: Cappozzo, M., “La collezione egizia del Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico ‘Luigi Pigorini’”, in *Bullettino di Paletnologia Italiana*, Roma, Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato, (2005–2007), 96: 131–202, cat. 73.

ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.name: *The Gate of the Roman*
ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.author: Athens 1985, no 205 (F-M Tsigakou)
ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.artist: Théodore Achille Louis, Vicomte du Moncel
ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.description2: Since King Otto (1833–1863) made efforts to transform immediately ruinous Athens into a European capital worthy of its erstwhile glory, around the mid-nineteenth century spectacular changes were made in the urban planning structure and morphology of the city. A reliable image of Athens at this time is given by Du Moncel in his book *Vues pittoresques des monuments d’Athenes*. This particular representation of Athens is the Roman Agora (Forum Romanum), natural continuation of the ancient Agora, was built c.10BC, the Gate of Athena Archegetis, which is depicted here. In Ottoman times this Roman gate was known as the Pazaroporta (Bazaar Gate), because it was used as the entrance to the bazaar, the commercial centre of Athens, which occupied the area between the Roman Agora and the Library of Hadrian.

en: Tsigakou, Fani-Maria, *British Images of Greece from the Benaki Museum Collections*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1995.

acb1417e-ded5-525f-a850-94113fa99185.name: Musée de Carthage
acb1417e-ded5-525f-a850-94113fa99185.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
acb1417e-ded5-525f-a850-94113fa99185.history: The museum was founded in 1875 on the premises of the Pères Blancs seminary, on the Byrsa Hill near the Saint-Louis Cathedral in Carthage. It was called the Musée Saint-Louis until 1899, and the Musée Lavigerie until 1956. It was given its current name by the Tunisian government following independence and the signing of the Modus Vivendi with the Catholic Church in 1964, at which point they relinquished all rights to the land.
acb1417e-ded5-525f-a850-94113fa99185.description2: The Musée de Carthage houses some of the most beautiful items from the Roman and Punic eras discovered on the Carthage archaeological site since the 19th century. After a long period of restoration, the museum also took on the findings from the UNESCO 1972–75 international arcehological campaign. It offered a new museographic approach, with each of the building's renovated rooms looking onto the beautiful landscape of Tunis Bay. The museum is thematically organised, with rooms dedicated to sculpture, amphoras, mosaics, or rooms reserved especially for works discovered by specific archaeological campaigns on the site.
